# ============================================================================
# Performance Comparison Utility
# ============================================================================

def compare_model_performance(models: dict, input_shape: tuple = (1, 5, 3, 64, 64)):
    """
    Compare performance of multiple models.
    
    Args:
        models: Dictionary of {name: model} pairs
        input_shape: Shape of input tensor for testing
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("MODEL PERFORMANCE COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    results = {}
    
    for name, model in models.items():
        print(f"\nTesting {name}...")
        
        # Count parameters
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        
        # Measure inference time
        benchmark = VideoGenerationBenchmark(model, device='cpu')
        test_input = torch.randn(*input_shape)
        timing_stats = benchmark.measure_inference_time(test_input, num_iterations=50)
        
        results[name] = {
            'total_params': total_params,
            'trainable_params': trainable_params,
            'inference_time_ms': timing_stats['mean'] * 1000,
            'fps': timing_stats['fps'],
            'param_memory_mb': total_params * 4 / (1024**2)
        }
    
    # Print comparison table
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"\n{'Model':<30} {'Params':<12} {'Time(ms)':<12} {'FPS':<10} {'Memory(MB)':<12}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for name, stats in results.items():
        print(f"{name:<30} {stats['total_params']:>11,} "
              f"{stats['inference_time_ms']:>11.2f} "
              f"{stats['fps']:>9.2f} "
              f"{stats['param_memory_mb']:>11.2f}")
    
    print("=" * 80)
    
    return results

class ExamplesGallery:
    """Collection of comprehensive usage examples."""
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_text_to_video_pipeline():
        """Complete text-to-video generation pipeline."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Complete Text-to-Video Pipeline")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # 1. Initialize model
        model = TextToVideoGenerator(
            vocab_size=50000,
            num_frames=16,
            frame_size=64
        )
        
        # 2. Prepare input
        text_description = "A cat playing with a ball in a garden"
        text_tokens = torch.randint(0, 50000, (1, 20))  # Simulated tokenization
        
        # 3. Generate video
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            video = model(text_tokens)
        
        print(f"Generated video shape: {video.shape}")
        print(f"Text: '{text_description}'")
        
        # 4. Evaluate quality
        stats = calculate_video_statistics(video)
        print(f"\nVideo Statistics:")
        for key, value in stats.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value:.4f}")
        
        return video
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_video_enhancement_pipeline():
        """Complete video enhancement pipeline."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Video Enhancement Pipeline")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # 1. Load low-quality video
        lr_video = torch.randn(1, 10, 3, 32, 32)
        print(f"Input video: {lr_video.shape}")
        
        # 2. Super-resolution
        sr_model = VideoSuperResolutionNetwork(scale_factor=4)
        sr_model.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            hr_video = sr_model(lr_video)
        
        print(f"After super-resolution: {hr_video.shape}")
        
        # 3. Temporal upsampling
        upsampler = TemporalUpsamplingNetwork(upsampling_factor=4)
        upsampler.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            smooth_video = upsampler(hr_video)
        
        print(f"After temporal upsampling: {smooth_video.shape}")
        
        # 4. Stabilization
        stabilizer = VideoStabilizationNetwork()
        stabilizer.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            final_video = stabilizer(smooth_video)
        
        print(f"Final enhanced video: {final_video.shape}")
        
        # 5. Quality comparison
        metrics = VideoQualityMetrics()
        temporal_consistency = metrics.temporal_consistency(final_video)
        print(f"\nFinal temporal consistency: {temporal_consistency:.6f}")
        
        return final_video
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_interactive_video_editing():
        """Interactive video editing example."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Interactive Video Editing")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # 1. Load original video
        original_video = torch.randn(1, 16, 3, 64, 64)
        print(f"Original video: {original_video.shape}")
        
        # 2. Inpainting (remove object)
        mask = torch.zeros(1, 16, 1, 64, 64)
        mask[:, :, :, 20:40, 20:40] = 1  # Mask center region
        
        inpainter = VideoInpaintingNetwork()
        inpainter.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            inpainted_video = inpainter(original_video, mask)
        
        print(f"After inpainting: {inpainted_video.shape}")
        
        # 3. Outpainting (extend canvas)
        outpainter = VideoOutpaintingNetwork(expansion_factor=1.5)
        outpainter.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            extended_video = outpainter(inpainted_video)
        
        print(f"After outpainting: {extended_video.shape}")
        
        # 4. Retargeting (change aspect ratio)
        retargeter = VideoRetargetingNetwork()
        retargeter.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            retargeted_video = retargeter(extended_video, target_size=(48, 80))
        
        print(f"After retargeting: {retargeted_video.shape}")
        
        return retargeted_video
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_motion_and_animation():
        """Motion transfer and animation example."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("EXAMPLE: Motion Transfer and Animation")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # 1. Prepare target appearance
        target_image = torch.randn(1, 3, 64, 64)
        print(f"Target appearance: {target_image.shape}")
        
        # 2. Prepare source motion
        source_keypoints = torch.randn(1, 20, 36)  # 18 keypoints * 2
        print(f"Source motion: {source_keypoints.shape}")
        
        # 3. Transfer motion
        motion_transfer = MotionTransferNetwork(num_keypoints=18)
        motion_transfer.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            animated_video = motion_transfer(target_image, source_keypoints)
        
        print(f"Animated video: {animated_video.shape}")
        
        # 4. Enhance with full-body synthesis
        pose_sequence = torch.randn(1, 20, 75)  # 25 joints * 3
        
        body_synth = FullBodyMotionSynthesizer(num_joints=25)
        body_synth.eval()
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            full_body_video = body_synth(pose_sequence)
        
        print(f"Full-body video: {full_body_video.shape}")
        
        return animated_video, full_body_video

def analyze_video_dataset(video_dir: str, num_samples: int = 100):
    """
    Analyze video dataset and compute statistics.
    
    Args:
        video_dir: Directory containing videos
        num_samples: Number of videos to sample for analysis
    """
    import os
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("VIDEO DATASET ANALYSIS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Get video files
    video_files = [
        f for f in os.listdir(video_dir)
        if f.endswith(('.mp4', '.avi', '.mov'))
    ][:num_samples]
    
    print(f"\nAnalyzing {len(video_files)} videos from {video_dir}")
    
    stats = {
        'total_videos': len(video_files),
        'resolutions': {},
        'durations': [],
        'frame_counts': [],
        'avg_fps': []
    }
    
    # Note: In practice, use actual video loading libraries
    print("\nDataset Statistics:")
    print(f"  Total Videos: {stats['total_videos']}")
    print("  (Use cv2.VideoCapture for actual analysis)")
    
    return stats


# ============================================================================
# Model Registry for Easy Access
# ============================================================================

class ModelRegistry:
    """
    Central registry for all video generation models.
    """
    
    _models = {
        'text_to_video': TextToVideoGenerator,
        'image_to_video': ImageToVideoGenerator,
        'video_interpolation': VideoInterpolator,
        'video_extrapolation': VideoExtrapolator,
        'video_prediction': VideoPredictionModel,
        'frame_prediction': FramePredictor,
        'long_term_prediction': LongTermVideoPredictor,
        'conditional_generation': ConditionalVideoGenerator,
        'action_conditioned': ActionConditionedVideoModel,
        'audio_driven': AudioDrivenVideoGenerator,
        'motion_transfer': MotionTransferNetwork,
        'video_retargeting': VideoRetargetingNetwork,
        'video_reenactment': VideoReenactmentNetwork,
        'talking_head': TalkingHeadGenerator,
        'motion_synthesis': FullBodyMotionSynthesizer,
        'video_inpainting': VideoInpaintingNetwork,
        'video_outpainting': VideoOutpaintingNetwork,
        'super_resolution': VideoSuperResolutionNetwork,
        'temporal_upsampling': TemporalUpsamplingNetwork,
        'video_stabilization': VideoStabilizationNetwork
    }
    
    @classmethod
    def list_models(cls) -> List[str]:
        """List all available models."""
        return list(cls._models.keys())
    
    @classmethod
    def get_model(cls, model_name: str, **kwargs) -> nn.Module:
        """
        Get model instance by name.
        
        Args:
            model_name: Name of the model
            **kwargs: Arguments to pass to model constructor
        Returns:
            Model instance
        """
        if model_name not in cls._models:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model '{model_name}' not found. "
                f"Available models: {cls.list_models()}"
            )
        
        model_class = cls._models[model_name]
        return model_class(**kwargs)
    
    @classmethod
    def get_model_info(cls, model_name: str) -> dict:
        """
        Get information about a model.
        
        Args:
            model_name: Name of the model
        Returns:
            Dictionary with model information
        """
        if model_name not in cls._models:
            raise ValueError(f"Model '{model_name}' not found")
        
        model_class = cls._models[model_name]
        
        return {
            'name': model_name,
            'class': model_class.__name__,
            'docstring': model_class.__doc__,
            'module': model_class.__module__
        }
    
    @classmethod
    def print_registry(cls):
        """Print all registered models with descriptions."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("MODEL REGISTRY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        for i, (name, model_class) in enumerate(cls._models.items(), 1):
            doc = model_class.__doc__ or "No description available"
            doc_first_line = doc.strip().split('\n')[0]
            print(f"\n{i:2d}. {name}")
            print(f"    Class: {model_class.__name__}")
            print(f"    Description: {doc_first_line}")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

💡 TIPS AND TRICKS

• Start with smaller resolutions (64x64) for faster experimentation
• Use mixed precision training to reduce memory usage
• Enable gradient checkpointing for larger models
• Batch your data appropriately based on GPU memory
• Use temporal coherence loss to reduce flickering
• Save checkpoints frequently during training
• Validate on a separate dataset to avoid overfitting


🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING

Problem: Out of memory during training
Solution: Reduce batch_size, use gradient checkpointing, or process fewer frames

Problem: Video has flickering/inconsistency
Solution: Increase temporal coherence loss weight, use ConvLSTM

Problem: Slow inference
Solution: Export to TorchScript, use quantization, or reduce model size

Problem: Poor quality results
Solution: Train longer, use perceptual loss, increase model capacity

    optional_packages = {

    missing_required = []
    missing_optional = []
    
    for package, name in required_packages.items():
        try:

            missing_required.append(name)
    
    for package, name in optional_packages.items():

    if missing_required:

## 1. Text-to-3D Generation Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Optional, Tuple, Dict
import numpy as np

class TextTo3DGenerator(nn.Module):
    """
    Text-to-3D generation using CLIP guidance and neural fields.
    Converts text descriptions into 3D representations.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        text_embed_dim: int = 512,
        hidden_dim: int = 256,
        num_layers: int = 8,
        grid_resolution: int = 64
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Text encoder (simplified - in practice use CLIP)
        self.text_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(text_embed_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
        )
        
        # Neural implicit field conditioned on text
        layers = []
        in_dim = 3 + hidden_dim  # 3D coordinates + text embedding
        for i in range(num_layers):
            out_dim = hidden_dim if i < num_layers - 1 else 4  # RGB + density
            layers.append(nn.Linear(in_dim, out_dim))
            if i < num_layers - 1:
                layers.append(nn.ReLU())
            in_dim = out_dim
        
        self.implicit_network = nn.ModuleList(layers)
        self.grid_resolution = grid_resolution
        
    def encode_text(self, text_features: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Encode text into conditioning vector."""
        return self.text_encoder(text_features)
    
    def query_implicit_field(
        self,
        coords: torch.Tensor,
        text_embedding: torch.Tensor
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Query the implicit field at given coordinates.
        
        Args:
            coords: (B, N, 3) 3D coordinates
            text_embedding: (B, D) text embedding
        
        Returns:
            rgb: (B, N, 3) RGB values
            density: (B, N, 1) density values
        """
        B, N, _ = coords.shape
        
        # Expand text embedding to match coordinates
        text_embed_expanded = text_embedding.unsqueeze(1).expand(B, N, -1)
        
        # Concatenate coordinates and text embedding
        x = torch.cat([coords, text_embed_expanded], dim=-1)
        
        # Pass through network
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.implicit_network):
            x = layer(x)
        
        # Split into RGB and density
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(x[..., :3])
        density = F.softplus(x[..., 3:4])
        
        return rgb, density
    
    def forward(
        self,
        text_features: torch.Tensor,
        num_samples: int = 64
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Generate 3D representation from text.
        
        Args:
            text_features: (B, text_embed_dim) text features
            num_samples: number of points to sample
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing 3D representation
        """
        B = text_features.shape[0]
        
        # Encode text
        text_embedding = self.encode_text(text_features)
        
        # Sample random 3D coordinates
        coords = torch.rand(B, num_samples, 3, device=text_features.device) * 2 - 1
        
        # Query implicit field
        rgb, density = self.query_implicit_field(coords, text_embedding)
        
        return {
            'coordinates': coords,
            'rgb': rgb,
            'density': density,
            'text_embedding': text_embedding
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = TextTo3DGenerator()
    text_features = torch.randn(2, 512)  # Batch of 2 text embeddings
    output = model(text_features, num_samples=1000)
    print(f"Generated 3D points: {output['coordinates'].shape}")
    print(f"RGB values: {output['rgb'].shape}")
    print(f"Density values: {output['density'].shape}")
```

## 2. Image-to-3D Reconstruction Pattern

```python
class ImageTo3DReconstructor(nn.Module):
    """
    Reconstructs 3D models from single or multiple images.
    Uses encoder-decoder architecture with 3D representation.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        image_size: int = 224,
        latent_dim: int = 512,
        grid_size: int = 32
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Image encoder (simplified ResNet-like)
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1),
            
            self._make_layer(64, 128, 2),
            self._make_layer(128, 256, 2),
            self._make_layer(256, 512, 2),
            
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(512, latent_dim)
        )
        
        # 3D decoder
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 256 * 4 * 4 * 4),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Unflatten(1, (256, 4, 4, 4)),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(256, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(64, 32, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv3d(32, 4, 3, padding=1)  # RGB + occupancy
        )
        
        self.grid_size = grid_size
    
    def _make_layer(self, in_channels, out_channels, num_blocks):
        """Helper to create residual blocks."""
        layers = []
        layers.append(nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, 3, stride=2, padding=1))
        layers.append(nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels))
        layers.append(nn.ReLU())
        
        for _ in range(num_blocks - 1):
            layers.append(nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, padding=1))
            layers.append(nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels))
            layers.append(nn.ReLU())
        
        return nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, images: torch.Tensor) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Reconstruct 3D from image(s).
        
        Args:
            images: (B, 3, H, W) input images
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with 3D voxel grid and features
        """
        # Encode image to latent
        latent = self.encoder(images)
        
        # Decode to 3D voxel grid
        voxel_grid = self.decoder(latent)
        
        # Split into RGB and occupancy
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, :3])
        occupancy = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, 3:4])
        
        return {
            'latent': latent,
            'voxel_rgb': rgb,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy,
            'voxel_grid': voxel_grid
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = ImageTo3DReconstructor()
    images = torch.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)
    output = model(images)
    print(f"Voxel RGB: {output['voxel_rgb'].shape}")
    print(f"Voxel occupancy: {output['voxel_occupancy'].shape}")
```

## 3. Video-to-3D Reconstruction Pattern

```python
class VideoTo3DReconstructor(nn.Module):
    """
    Reconstructs 3D models from video sequences.
    Aggregates temporal information for better reconstruction.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        image_size: int = 224,
        latent_dim: int = 512,
        hidden_dim: int = 256,
        num_frames: int = 16
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Spatial feature extractor per frame
        self.spatial_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Flatten()
        )
        
        # Temporal aggregation with LSTM
        self.temporal_aggregator = nn.LSTM(
            input_size=256,
            hidden_size=hidden_dim,
            num_layers=2,
            batch_first=True,
            bidirectional=True
        )
        
        # 3D reconstruction head
        self.reconstruction_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 2, latent_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 256 * 8 * 8 * 8),
            nn.ReLU()
        )
        
        # 3D upsampling
        self.upsample_3d = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Unflatten(1, (256, 8, 8, 8)),
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(256, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv3d(64, 4, 3, padding=1)
        )
        
        self.num_frames = num_frames
    
    def forward(self, video: torch.Tensor) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Reconstruct 3D from video.
        
        Args:
            video: (B, T, 3, H, W) video frames
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with 3D reconstruction
        """
        B, T, C, H, W = video.shape
        
        # Extract spatial features per frame
        video_flat = video.view(B * T, C, H, W)
        spatial_features = self.spatial_encoder(video_flat)
        spatial_features = spatial_features.view(B, T, -1)
        
        # Aggregate temporal information
        temporal_features, (h_n, c_n) = self.temporal_aggregator(spatial_features)
        
        # Use final hidden state for reconstruction
        aggregated = temporal_features[:, -1, :]
        
        # Reconstruct 3D
        latent = self.reconstruction_head(aggregated)
        voxel_grid = self.upsample_3d(latent)
        
        # Split into components
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, :3])
        occupancy = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, 3:4])
        
        return {
            'spatial_features': spatial_features,
            'temporal_features': temporal_features,
            'voxel_rgb': rgb,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = VideoTo3DReconstructor()
    video = torch.randn(2, 16, 3, 224, 224)  # 2 videos, 16 frames each
    output = model(video)
    print(f"Voxel RGB: {output['voxel_rgb'].shape}")
    print(f"Temporal features: {output['temporal_features'].shape}")
```

## 4. Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Pattern

```python
class MultiView3DReconstructor(nn.Module):
    """
    Reconstructs 3D from multiple views with known camera poses.
    Uses feature fusion and geometric reasoning.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        image_size: int = 224,
        feature_dim: int = 256,
        grid_resolution: int = 64
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Per-view feature extractor
        self.view_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(256, feature_dim, 3, padding=1)
        )
        
        # Cross-view attention
        self.cross_view_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=feature_dim,
            num_heads=8,
            batch_first=True
        )
        
        # 3D volume decoder
        self.volume_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(feature_dim, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(64, 32, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv3d(32, 4, 3, padding=1)
        )
        
        self.grid_resolution = grid_resolution
    
    def project_features_to_3d(
        self,
        features: torch.Tensor,
        camera_matrices: torch.Tensor,
        grid_coords: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Project 2D features to 3D
```python
        Project 2D features to 3D grid using camera projection.
        
        Args:
            features: (B, V, C, H, W) multi-view features
            camera_matrices: (B, V, 3, 4) camera projection matrices
            grid_coords: (B, D, H, W, 3) 3D grid coordinates
        
        Returns:
            Projected features in 3D space
        """
        B, V, C, H, W = features.shape
        
        # Simplified projection (in practice, use proper camera geometry)
        # Average features across views
        aggregated_features = features.mean(dim=1)  # (B, C, H, W)
        
        # Reshape to 3D volume
        volume_features = aggregated_features.unsqueeze(2).repeat(1, 1, 8, 1, 1)
        
        return volume_features
    
    def forward(
        self,
        images: torch.Tensor,
        camera_matrices: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Reconstruct 3D from multiple views.
        
        Args:
            images: (B, V, 3, H, W) multi-view images
            camera_matrices: (B, V, 3, 4) optional camera matrices
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with 3D reconstruction
        """
        B, V, C, H, W = images.shape
        
        # Extract features per view
        images_flat = images.view(B * V, C, H, W)
        features_flat = self.view_encoder(images_flat)
        _, C_feat, H_feat, W_feat = features_flat.shape
        features = features_flat.view(B, V, C_feat, H_feat, W_feat)
        
        # Flatten spatial dimensions for attention
        features_for_attn = features.view(B, V, C_feat, -1).permute(0, 1, 3, 2)
        features_for_attn = features_for_attn.reshape(B, V * H_feat * W_feat, C_feat)
        
        # Cross-view attention
        attended_features, attn_weights = self.cross_view_attention(
            features_for_attn,
            features_for_attn,
            features_for_attn
        )
        
        # Reshape back
        attended_features = attended_features.view(B, V, H_feat * W_feat, C_feat)
        attended_features = attended_features.mean(dim=1)  # Aggregate views
        attended_features = attended_features.view(B, C_feat, H_feat, W_feat)
        
        # Create 3D grid coordinates
        grid_coords = torch.stack(torch.meshgrid(
            torch.linspace(-1, 1, 8),
            torch.linspace(-1, 1, H_feat),
            torch.linspace(-1, 1, W_feat),
            indexing='ij'
        ), dim=-1).to(images.device)
        
        # Project to 3D
        volume_features = self.project_features_to_3d(
            features, camera_matrices, grid_coords
        )
        
        # Decode to 3D voxels
        voxel_grid = self.volume_decoder(volume_features)
        
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, :3])
        occupancy = torch.sigmoid(voxel_grid[:, 3:4])
        
        return {
            'view_features': features,
            'voxel_rgb': rgb,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy,
            'attention_weights': attn_weights
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = MultiView3DReconstructor()
    images = torch.randn(2, 4, 3, 224, 224)  # 2 batches, 4 views each
    output = model(images)
    print(f"Voxel RGB: {output['voxel_rgb'].shape}")
    print(f"Attention weights: {output['attention_weights'].shape}")

## 5. Single-View 3D Reconstruction Pattern

```python
class SingleView3DReconstructor(nn.Module):
    """
    Reconstructs 3D from a single image using learned priors.
    Uses shape and appearance priors learned from data.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        image_size: int = 224,
        latent_dim: int = 512,
        num_categories: int = 10
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Image encoder with category prediction
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1),
            
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv2d(256, 512, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Flatten()
        )
        
        # Category classifier (helps with shape priors)
        self.category_head = nn.Linear(512, num_categories)
        
        # Shape latent predictor
        self.shape_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(512, latent_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        # Texture latent predictor
        self.texture_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(512, latent_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        # 3D shape decoder
        self.shape_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 256 * 4 * 4 * 4),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Unflatten(1, (256, 4, 4, 4)),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(256, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(64, 32, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv3d(32, 1, 3, padding=1)  # Occupancy only
        )
        
        # Texture decoder
        self.texture_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 256 * 4 * 4 * 4),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Unflatten(1, (256, 4, 4, 4)),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(256, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(64, 32, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv3d(32, 3, 3, padding=1)  # RGB
        )
        
    def forward(self, image: torch.Tensor) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Reconstruct 3D from single image.
        
        Args:
            image: (B, 3, H, W) input image
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with 3D reconstruction and predictions
        """
        # Encode image
        features = self.encoder(image)
        
        # Predict category
        category_logits = self.category_head(features)
        
        # Predict shape and texture latents
        shape_latent = self.shape_head(features)
        texture_latent = self.texture_head(features)
        
        # Decode to 3D
        occupancy = torch.sigmoid(self.shape_decoder(shape_latent))
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(self.texture_decoder(texture_latent))
        
        return {
            'category_logits': category_logits,
            'shape_latent': shape_latent,
            'texture_latent': texture_latent,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy,
            'voxel_rgb': rgb
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = SingleView3DReconstructor()
    image = torch.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)
    output = model(image)
    print(f"Category logits: {output['category_logits'].shape}")
    print(f"Voxel occupancy: {output['voxel_occupancy'].shape}")
    print(f"Voxel RGB: {output['voxel_rgb'].shape}")
```

## 6. Neural Implicit 3D Pattern

```python
class NeuralImplicit3D(nn.Module):
    """
    Neural implicit 3D representation using coordinate-based MLPs.
    Represents 3D shapes as continuous functions.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        hidden_dim: int = 256,
        num_layers: int = 8,
        skip_connections: list = [4],
        use_positional_encoding: bool = True,
        num_frequencies: int = 10
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.use_positional_encoding = use_positional_encoding
        self.num_frequencies = num_frequencies
        
        # Calculate input dimension
        if use_positional_encoding:
            input_dim = 3 * (2 * num_frequencies + 1)  # Positional encoding
        else:
            input_dim = 3
        
        # Build MLP with skip connections
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
        self.skip_connections = skip_connections
        
        for i in range(num_layers):
            if i == 0:
                layer = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
            elif i in skip_connections:
                layer = nn.Linear(hidden_dim + input_dim, hidden_dim)
            else:
                layer = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
            
            self.layers.append(layer)
        
        # Output layers
        self.sdf_head = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1)  # Signed distance
        self.color_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, 3)
        )
        
    def positional_encoding(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply positional encoding to coordinates.
        
        Args:
            x: (B, N, 3) input coordinates
        
        Returns:
            Encoded coordinates
        """
        if not self.use_positional_encoding:
            return x
        
        # Generate frequency bands
        freq_bands = 2.0 ** torch.linspace(
            0, self.num_frequencies - 1,
            self.num_frequencies,
            device=x.device
        )
        
        encoded = [x]
        for freq in freq_bands:
            encoded.append(torch.sin(freq * np.pi * x))
            encoded.append(torch.cos(freq * np.pi * x))
        
        return torch.cat(encoded, dim=-1)
    
    def forward(
        self,
        coords: torch.Tensor,
        return_features: bool = False
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Query implicit function at coordinates.
        
        Args:
            coords: (B, N, 3) query coordinates
            return_features: whether to return intermediate features
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with SDF and color predictions
        """
        # Apply positional encoding
        x = self.positional_encoding(coords)
        input_encoding = x
        
        # Forward through MLP
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
            if i in self.skip_connections:
                x = torch.cat([x, input_encoding], dim=-1)
            
            x = layer(x)
            
            if i < len(self.layers) - 1:
                x = F.relu(x)
        
        # Predict SDF and color
        sdf = self.sdf_head(x)
        color = torch.sigmoid(self.color_head(x))
        
        result = {
            'sdf': sdf,
            'color': color
        }
        
        if return_features:
            result['features'] = x
        
        return result
    
    def extract_mesh(
        self,
        resolution: int = 128,
        threshold: float = 0.0
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Extract mesh using marching cubes (simplified).
        
        Args:
            resolution: grid resolution
            threshold: SDF threshold for surface
        
        Returns:
            vertices and colors
        """
        # Create grid
        x = torch.linspace(-1, 1, resolution)
        y = torch.linspace(-1, 1, resolution)
        z = torch.linspace(-1, 1, resolution)
        
        xx, yy, zz = torch.meshgrid(x, y, z, indexing='ij')
        coords = torch.stack([xx, yy, zz], dim=-1).reshape(-1, 3)
        
        # Query SDF in batches
        batch_size = 10000
        sdf_values = []
        colors = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i in range(0, len(coords), batch_size):
                batch_coords = coords[i:i+batch_size].unsqueeze(0)
                output = self.forward(batch_coords)
                sdf_values.append(output['sdf'].squeeze(0))
                colors.append(output['color'].squeeze(0))
        
        sdf_grid = torch.cat(sdf_values, dim=0).reshape(resolution, resolution, resolution)
        color_grid = torch.cat(colors, dim=0).reshape(resolution, resolution, resolution, 3)
        
        # Extract surface points (simplified - proper marching cubes needed)
        surface_mask = (sdf_grid.abs() < 0.01)
        surface_coords = coords[surface_mask.flatten()]
        surface_colors = color_grid.reshape(-1, 3)[surface_mask.flatten()]
        
        return surface_coords, surface_colors

    coords = torch.rand(1, 1000, 3) * 2 - 1  # Random points in [-1

## 7. Explicit 3D Representation Pattern

```python
class Explicit3DRepresentation(nn.Module):
    """
    Explicit 3D representation using voxels, meshes, or point clouds.
    Direct storage and manipulation of 3D geometry.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        representation_type: str = 'voxel',  # 'voxel', 'mesh', 'pointcloud'
        resolution: int = 64,
        num_points: int = 2048,
        feature_dim: int = 256
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.representation_type = representation_type
        self.resolution = resolution
        self.num_points = num_points
        
        # Encoder for input processing
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(128, 256, 3, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(256, feature_dim)
        )
        
        if representation_type == 'voxel':
            self._init_voxel_decoder(feature_dim)
        elif representation_type == 'pointcloud':
            self._init_pointcloud_decoder(feature_dim)
        elif representation_type == 'mesh':
            self._init_mesh_decoder(feature_dim)
    
    def _init_voxel_decoder(self, feature_dim):
        """Initialize voxel-based decoder."""
        self.voxel_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, 256 * 4 * 4 * 4),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Unflatten(1, (256, 4, 4, 4)),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(256, 128, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(128, 64, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(64, 32, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.ConvTranspose3d(32, 16, 4, stride=2, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(16),
            nn.ReLU(),
            
            nn.Conv3d(16, 4, 3, padding=1)  # RGB + occupancy
        )
    
    def _init_pointcloud_decoder(self, feature_dim):
        """Initialize point cloud decoder."""
        self.pointcloud_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 1024),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(1024, self.num_points * 3)  # XYZ coordinates
        )
        
        self.pointcloud_feature_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 1024),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(1024, self.num_points * 3)  # RGB colors
        )
    
    def _init_mesh_decoder(self, feature_dim):
        """Initialize mesh decoder with deformable template."""
        # Start with a sphere template
        self.register_buffer('template_vertices', self._create_sphere_template())
        num_vertices = self.template_vertices.shape[0]
        
        self.vertex_offset_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 1024),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(1024, num_vertices * 3)
        )
        
        self.vertex_color_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, num_vertices * 3)
        )
    
    def _create_sphere_template(self, subdivisions: int = 2):
        """Create icosphere template mesh."""
        # Simplified icosphere vertices (you'd use a proper mesh library)
        t = (1.0 + np.sqrt(5.0)) / 2.0
        vertices = torch.tensor([
            [-1, t, 0], [1, t, 0], [-1, -t, 0], [1, -t, 0],
            [0, -1, t], [0, 1, t], [0, -1, -t], [0, 1, -t],
            [t, 0, -1], [t, 0, 1], [-t, 0, -1], [-t, 0, 1]
        ], dtype=torch.float32)
        
        # Normalize
        vertices = F.normalize(vertices, dim=1)
        return vertices
    
    def forward(self, input_data: torch.Tensor) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Generate explicit 3D representation.
        
        Args:
            input_data: (B, 3, H, W) input images
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with 3D representation
        """
        # Encode input
        features = self.encoder(input_data)
        
        if self.representation_type == 'voxel':
            return self._forward_voxel(features)
        elif self.representation_type == 'pointcloud':
            return self._forward_pointcloud(features)
        elif self.representation_type == 'mesh':
            return self._forward_mesh(features)
    
    def _forward_voxel(self, features):
        """Generate voxel representation."""
        voxels = self.voxel_decoder(features)
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(voxels[:, :3])
        occupancy = torch.sigmoid(voxels[:, 3:4])
        
        return {
            'type': 'voxel',
            'voxel_rgb': rgb,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy,
            'features': features
        }
    
    def _forward_pointcloud(self, features):
        """Generate point cloud representation."""
        B = features.shape[0]
        
        coords = self.pointcloud_decoder(features)
        coords = coords.view(B, self.num_points, 3)
        coords = torch.tanh(coords)  # Normalize to [-1, 1]
        
        colors = self.pointcloud_feature_decoder(features)
        colors = colors.view(B, self.num_points, 3)
        colors = torch.sigmoid(colors)
        
        return {
            'type': 'pointcloud',
            'points': coords,
            'colors': colors,
            'features': features
        }
    
    def _forward_mesh(self, features):
        """Generate mesh representation."""
        B = features.shape[0]
        num_vertices = self.template_vertices.shape[0]
        
        # Predict vertex offsets
        offsets = self.vertex_offset_decoder(features)
        offsets = offsets.view(B, num_vertices, 3)
        
        # Deform template
        vertices = self.template_vertices.unsqueeze(0) + offsets * 0.3
        
        # Predict colors
        colors = self.vertex_color_decoder(features)
        colors = colors.view(B, num_vertices, 3)
        colors = torch.sigmoid(colors)
        
        return {
            'type': 'mesh',
            'vertices': vertices,
            'colors': colors,
            'template': self.template_vertices,
            'features': features
        }


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Voxel representation
    voxel_model = Explicit3DRepresentation(representation_type='voxel')
    images = torch.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)
    voxel_output = voxel_model(images)
    print(f"Voxel RGB: {voxel_output['voxel_rgb'].shape}")
    
    # Point cloud representation
    pc_model = Explicit3DRepresentation(representation_type='pointcloud')
    pc_output = pc_model(images)
    print(f"Point cloud: {pc_output['points'].shape}")
    
    # Mesh representation
    mesh_model = Explicit3DRepresentation(representation_type='mesh')
    mesh_output = mesh_model(images)
    print(f"Mesh vertices: {mesh_output['vertices'].shape}")
```

## 8. Voxel-Based 3D Pattern

```python
class VoxelBased3D(nn.Module):
    """
    Voxel-based 3D representation with hierarchical processing.
    Supports multi-resolution voxel grids.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        base_resolution: int = 32,
        num_levels: int = 3,
        feature_dim: int = 64,
        use_octree: bool = False
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.base_resolution = base_resolution
        self.num_levels = num_levels
        self.use_octree = use_octree
        
        # Multi-scale voxel encoders
        self.voxel_encoders = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(num_levels):
            resolution = base_resolution * (2 ** i)
            self.voxel_encoders.append(
                nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv3d(4, feature_dim, 3, padding=1),  # RGBA input
                    nn.BatchNorm3d(feature_dim),
                    nn.ReLU(),
                    nn.Conv3d(feature_dim, feature_dim, 3, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm3d(feature_dim),
                    nn.ReLU()
                )
            )
        
        # Feature fusion across scales
        self.fusion_layers = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(num_levels - 1):
            self.fusion_layers.append(
                nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv3d(feature_dim * 2, feature_dim, 1),
                    nn.BatchNorm3d(feature_dim),
                    nn.ReLU()
                )
            )
        
        # Voxel refinement network
        self.refinement = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv3d(feature_dim, feature_dim, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(feature_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv3d(feature_dim, feature_dim, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm3d(feature_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv3d(feature_dim, 4, 1)  # Output RGBA
        )
        
        # Occupancy prediction head
        self.occupancy_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv3d(feature_dim, 32, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv3d(32, 1, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def create_voxel_grid(
        self,
        batch_size: int,
        resolution: int,
        device: torch.device
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Create empty voxel grid."""
        return torch.zeros(
            batch_size, 4, resolution, resolution, resolution,
            device=device
        )
    
    def upsample_voxels(
        self,
        voxels: torch.Tensor,
        scale_factor: int = 2
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Upsample voxel grid."""
        return F.interpolate(
            voxels,
            scale_factor=scale_factor,
            mode='trilinear',
            align_corners=False
        )
    
    def forward(
        self,
        input_voxels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        batch_size: int = 1
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Process voxel grid hierarchically.
        
        Args:
            input_voxels: (B, 4, D, H, W) input voxel grid or None
            batch_size: batch size if input_voxels is None
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with multi-scale voxel representations
        """
        device = input_voxels.device if input_voxels is not None else torch.device('cpu')
        
        # Create or use input voxels
        if input_voxels is None:
            current_voxels = self.create_voxel_grid(
                batch_size,
                self.base_resolution,
                device
            )
        else:
            current_voxels = input_voxels
        
        # Multi-scale processing
        multi_scale_features = []
        multi_scale_voxels = []
        
        for level in range(self.num_levels):
            # Encode current level
            features = self.voxel_encoders[level](current_voxels)
            multi_scale_features.append(features)
            multi_scale_voxels.append(current_voxels)
            
            # Upsample for next level
            if level < self.num_levels - 1:
                current_voxels = self.upsample_voxels(current_voxels)
        
        # Hierarchical feature fusion (top-down)
        fused_features = multi_scale_features[-1]
        
        for level in range(self.num_levels - 2, -1, -1):
            # Downsample higher level features
            downsampled = F.interpolate(
                fused_features,
                size=multi_scale_features[level].shape[2:],
                mode='trilinear',
                align_corners=False
            )
            
            # Fuse with current level
            concatenated = torch.cat([
                multi_scale_features[level],
                downsampled
            ], dim=1)
            
            fused_features = self.fusion_layers[level](concatenated)
        
        # Refine voxels
        refined_voxels = self.refinement(fused_features)
        rgb = torch.sigmoid(refined_voxels[:, :3])
        alpha = torch.sigmoid(refined_voxels[:, 3:4])
        
        # Predict occupancy
        occupancy = self.occupancy_head(fused_features)
        
        return {
            'voxel
```python
        return {
            'voxel_rgb': rgb,
            'voxel_alpha': alpha,
            'voxel_occupancy': occupancy,
            'multi_scale_features': multi_scale_features,
            'multi_scale_voxels': multi_scale_voxels,
            'fused_features': fused_features
        }
    
    def extract_surface_voxels(
        self,
        occupancy: torch.Tensor,
        threshold: float = 0.5
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Extract surface voxels based on occupancy."""
        # Compute gradient to find surface
        grad_x = occupancy[:, :, 1:, :, :] - occupancy[:, :, :-1, :, :]
        grad_y = occupancy[:, :, :, 1:, :] - occupancy[:, :, :, :-1, :]
        grad_z = occupancy[:, :, :, :, 1:] - occupancy[:, :, :, :, :-1]
        
        # Pad gradients
        grad_x = F.pad(grad_x, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))
        grad_y = F.pad(grad_y, (0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0))
        grad_z = F.pad(grad_z, (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0))
        
        # Surface is where gradient magnitude is high
        gradient_magnitude = torch.sqrt(grad_x**2 + grad_y**2 + grad_z**2)
        surface_mask = (gradient_magnitude > 0.1) & (occupancy > threshold)
        
        return surface_mask

    print(f"Voxel occupancy: {output['voxel_occupancy'].shape}")
    print(f"Number of scales: {len(output['multi_scale_features'])}")
    
    # Extract surface
    surface_mask = model.extract_surface_voxels(output['voxel_occupancy'])
    print(f"Surface mask: {surface_mask.shape}")

## 9. Point Cloud Generation Pattern

```python
class PointCloudGenerator(nn.Module):
    """
    Generates 3D point clouds with features.
    Supports conditional generation and refinement.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        latent_dim: int = 512,
        num_points: int = 2048,
        feature_dim: int = 128,
        use_folding: bool = True
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_points = num_points
        self.use_folding = use_folding
        
        # Latent to point cloud decoder
        self.initial_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 1024),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(1024, num_points * 3)
        )
        
        # Per-point feature decoder
        self.feature_decoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, 1024),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(1024, num_points * feature_dim)
        )
        
        if use_folding:
            # Folding-based decoder for smoother surfaces
            self.folding_layer1 = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv1d(3 + latent_dim, 512, 1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Conv1d(512, 256, 1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Conv1d(256, 3, 1)
            )
            
            self.folding_layer2 = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv1d(3 + latent_dim, 512, 1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Conv1d(512, 256, 1),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Conv1d(256, 3, 1)
            )
        
        # Point refinement network
        self.refinement = PointNetPlusPlus(
            in_channels=3 + feature_dim,
            out_channels=3
        )
        
        # Color prediction
        self.color_predictor = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(feature_dim, 128, 1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv1d(128, 64, 1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv1d(64, 3, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def create_2d_grid(self, grid_size: int = 45) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Create 2D grid for folding decoder."""
        x = torch.linspace(-1, 1, grid_size)
        y = torch.linspace(-1, 1, grid_size)
        grid_x, grid_y = torch.meshgrid(x, y, indexing='ij')
        grid = torch.stack([grid_x, grid_y], dim=-1)
        grid = grid.reshape(-1, 2)
        
        # Pad to 3D
        grid = F.pad(grid, (0, 1), value=0)
        return grid
    
    def forward(
        self,
        latent: torch.Tensor,
        return_intermediate: bool = False
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Generate point cloud from latent code.
        
        Args:
            latent: (B, latent_dim) latent code
            return_intermediate: whether to return intermediate results
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with point cloud and features
        """
        B = latent.shape[0]
        
        if self.use_folding:
            # Folding-based generation
            grid = self.create_2d_grid().to(latent.device)
            grid = grid.unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1, -1).transpose(1, 2)
            
            # Expand latent
            latent_expanded = latent.unsqueeze(2).expand(-1, -1, grid.shape[2])
            
            # First folding
            folding_input1 = torch.cat([grid, latent_expanded], dim=1)
            folded1 = self.folding_layer1(folding_input1)
            
            # Second folding
            folding_input2 = torch.cat([folded1, latent_expanded], dim=1)
            points = self.folding_layer2(folding_input2)
            points = points.transpose(1, 2)
            
            # Subsample to target number of points
            if points.shape[1] > self.num_points:
                indices = torch.randperm(points.shape[1])[:self.num_points]
                points = points[:, indices, :]
        else:
            # Direct generation
            points = self.initial_decoder(latent)
            points = points.view(B, self.num_points, 3)
            points = torch.tanh(points)
        
        # Generate per-point features
        features = self.feature_decoder(latent)
        features = features.view(B, self.num_points, -1)
        
        # Refine points
        points_with_features = torch.cat([points, features], dim=-1)
        point_offsets = self.refinement(points_with_features.transpose(1, 2))
        refined_points = points + point_offsets.transpose(1, 2) * 0.1
        
        # Predict colors
        colors = self.color_predictor(features.transpose(1, 2))
        colors = colors.transpose(1, 2)
        
        result = {
            'points': refined_points,
            'colors': colors,
            'features': features
        }
        
        if return_intermediate:
            result['initial_points'] = points
            result['point_offsets'] = point_offsets.transpose(1, 2)
        
        return result


class PointNetPlusPlus(nn.Module):
    """Simplified PointNet++ for point cloud processing."""
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv1d(in_channels, 128, 1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv1d(128, 256, 1)
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv1d(256, 512, 1)
        self.conv4 = nn.Conv1d(512, 256, 1)
        self.conv5 = nn.Conv1d(256, out_channels, 1)
        
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(128)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm1d(256)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm1d(512)
        self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm1d(256)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Process point cloud features."""
        x = F.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn3(self.conv3(x)))
        x = F.relu(self.bn4(self.conv4(x)))
        x = self.conv5(x)
        return x


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = PointCloudGenerator(num_points=2048, use_folding=True)
    latent = torch.randn(2, 512)
    
    output = model(latent, return_intermediate=True)
    print(f"Generated points: {output['points'].shape}")
    print(f"Point colors: {output['colors'].shape}")
    print(f"Point features: {output['features'].shape}")

## 10. Mesh Generation Pattern

```python
class MeshGenerator(nn.Module):
    """
    Generates 3D meshes using deformable templates or learned vertices.
    Supports topology-preserving deformations.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        latent_dim: int = 512,
        num_vertices: int = 642,  # Icosphere subdivision level 2
        use_graph_conv: bool = True
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_vertices = num_vertices
        
        # Create template mesh (icosphere)
        vertices, faces = self._create_icosphere(subdivisions=2)
        self.register_buffer('template_vertices', vertices)
        self.register_buffer('faces', faces)
        
        # Build adjacency for graph convolution
        if use_graph_conv:
            adjacency = self._build_adjacency(faces, num_vertices)
            self.register_buffer('adjacency', adjacency)
        
        # Latent to vertex features
        self.latent_projector = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(512, num_vertices * 64)
        )
        
        if use_graph_conv:
            # Graph convolutional layers
            self.graph_conv1 = GraphConvolution(64, 128)
            self.graph_conv2 = GraphConvolution(128, 256)
            self.graph_conv3 = GraphConvolution(256, 128)
        else:
            # MLP per vertex
            self.vertex_mlp = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(64, 128),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Linear(128, 256),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Linear(256, 128),
                nn.ReLU()
            )
        
        # Vertex displacement predictor
        self.displacement_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 3),
            nn.Tanh()
        )
        
        # Vertex color predictor
        self.color_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 3),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.use_graph_conv = use_graph_conv
    
    def _create_icosphere(
        self,
        subdivisions: int = 2
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Create icosphere mesh."""
        # Golden ratio
        t = (1.0 + np.sqrt(5.0)) / 2.0
        
        # Initial icosahedron vertices
        vertices = torch.tensor([
            [-1, t, 0], [1, t, 0], [-1, -t, 0], [1, -t, 0],
            [0, -1, t], [0, 1, t], [0, -1, -t], [0, 1, -t],
            [t, 0, -1], [t, 0, 1], [-t, 0, -1], [-t, 0, 1]
        ], dtype=torch.float32)
        
        # Normalize to unit sphere
        vertices = F.normalize(vertices, dim=1)
        
        # Initial faces
        faces = torch.tensor([
            [0, 11, 5], [0, 5, 1], [0, 1, 7], [0, 7, 10], [0, 10, 11],
            [1, 5, 9], [5, 11, 4], [11, 10, 2], [10, 7, 6], [7, 1, 8],
            [3, 9, 4], [3, 4, 2], [3, 2, 6], [3, 6, 8], [3, 8, 9],
            [4, 9, 5], [2, 4, 11], [6, 2, 10], [8, 6, 7], [9, 8, 1]
        ], dtype=torch.long)
        
        # Subdivide
        for _ in range(subdivisions):
            vertices, faces = self._subdivide_mesh(vertices, faces)
        
        return vertices, faces
    
    def _subdivide_mesh(
        self,
        vertices: torch.Tensor,
        faces: torch.Tensor
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Subdivide mesh by splitting each triangle into 4."""
        edge_to_vertex = {}
        new_vertices = vertices.clone()
        new_faces = []
        
        def get_middle_vertex(v1_idx, v2_idx):
            edge = tuple(sorted([v1_idx, v2_idx]))
            if edge not in edge_to_vertex:
                v1 = vertices[v1_idx]
                v2 = vertices[v2_idx]
                middle = (v1 + v2) / 2
                middle = F.normalize(middle.unsqueeze(0), dim=1).squeeze(0)
                
                edge_to_vertex[edge] = len
```python
                edge_to_vertex[edge] = len(new_vertices)
                new_vertices = torch.cat([new_vertices, middle.unsqueeze(0)], dim=0)
            
            return edge_to_vertex[edge]
        
        # Subdivide each face
        for face in faces:
            v1, v2, v3 = face.tolist()
            
            # Get middle vertices
            a = get_middle_vertex(v1, v2)
            b = get_middle_vertex(v2, v3)
            c = get_middle_vertex(v3, v1)
            
            # Create 4 new faces
            new_faces.extend([
                [v1, a, c],
                [v2, b, a],
                [v3, c, b],
                [a, b, c]
            ])
        
        new_faces = torch.tensor(new_faces, dtype=torch.long)
        return new_vertices, new_faces
    
    def _build_adjacency(
        self,
        faces: torch.Tensor,
        num_vertices: int
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Build adjacency matrix from faces."""
        adjacency = torch.zeros(num_vertices, num_vertices)
        
        for face in faces:
            v1, v2, v3 = face.tolist()
            adjacency[v1, v2] = adjacency[v2, v1] = 1
            adjacency[v2, v3] = adjacency[v3, v2] = 1
            adjacency[v3, v1] = adjacency[v1, v3] = 1
        
        # Add self-loops
        adjacency += torch.eye(num_vertices)
        
        # Normalize
        degree = adjacency.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        adjacency = adjacency / degree
        
        return adjacency
    
    def forward(
        self,
        latent: torch.Tensor,
        deformation_scale: float = 0.5
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Generate mesh from latent code.
        
        Args:
            latent: (B, latent_dim) latent code
            deformation_scale: scale of deformations
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with mesh vertices, faces, and colors
        """
        B = latent.shape[0]
        
        # Project latent to vertex features
        vertex_features = self.latent_projector(latent)
        vertex_features = vertex_features.view(B, self.num_vertices, -1)
        
        if self.use_graph_conv:
            # Apply graph convolutions
            x = vertex_features
            x = F.relu(self.graph_conv1(x, self.adjacency))
            x = F.relu(self.graph_conv2(x, self.adjacency))
            x = F.relu(self.graph_conv3(x, self.adjacency))
        else:
            # Apply MLP
            x = self.vertex_mlp(vertex_features)
        
        # Predict displacements
        displacements = self.displacement_head(x) * deformation_scale
        
        # Predict colors
        colors = self.color_head(x)
        
        # Deform template
        template_expanded = self.template_vertices.unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1, -1)
        vertices = template_expanded + displacements
        
        # Normalize to sphere (optional, maintains topology)
        vertices = F.normalize(vertices, dim=2)
        
        return {
            'vertices': vertices,
            'faces': self.faces,
            'colors': colors,
            'displacements': displacements,
            'template_vertices': self.template_vertices,
            'vertex_features': x
        }
    
    def compute_mesh_normals(
        self,
        vertices: torch.Tensor,
        faces: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Compute per-vertex normals."""
        B, V, _ = vertices.shape
        normals = torch.zeros_like(vertices)
        
        # Get face vertices
        v1 = vertices[:, faces[:, 0]]
        v2 = vertices[:, faces[:, 1]]
        v3 = vertices[:, faces[:, 2]]
        
        # Compute face normals
        face_normals = torch.cross(v2 - v1, v3 - v1, dim=2)
        face_normals = F.normalize(face_normals, dim=2)
        
        # Accumulate to vertices
        for i in range(3):
            normals.scatter_add_(1, faces[:, i:i+1].expand(B, -1, 3), face_normals)
        
        # Normalize
        normals = F.normalize(normals, dim=2)
        
        return normals


class GraphConvolution(nn.Module):
    """Graph convolution layer for mesh processing."""
    def __init__(self, in_features: int, out_features: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)
    
    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        adjacency: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply graph convolution.
        
        Args:
            x: (B, V, in_features) vertex features
            adjacency: (V, V) adjacency matrix
        
        Returns:
            (B, V, out_features) convolved features
        """
        # Aggregate neighbor features
        x = torch.matmul(adjacency, x)
        
        # Apply linear transformation
        x = self.linear(x)
        
        return x


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = MeshGenerator(num_vertices=642, use_graph_conv=True)
    latent = torch.randn(2, 512)
    
    output = model(latent)
    print(f"Mesh vertices: {output['vertices'].shape}")
    print(f"Mesh faces: {output['faces'].shape}")
    print(f"Vertex colors: {output['colors'].shape}")
    
    # Compute normals
    normals = model.compute_mesh_normals(output['vertices'], output['faces'])
    print(f"Vertex normals: {normals.shape}")
