# 2327. Image-to-Text Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class ImageToTextAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns image features to text for caption generation/retrieval.
    Uses visual attention over text tokens.
    """
    def __init__(self, image_dim: int = 2048, text_dim: int = 768,
                 hidden_dim: int = 512, vocab_size: int = 30000):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Image feature encoder
        self.image_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(image_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        )
        
        # Text embedding
        self.text_embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, text_dim)
        
        # Image-guided text decoder
        self.decoder = nn.TransformerDecoder(
            nn.TransformerDecoderLayer(d_model=text_dim, nhead=8),
            num_layers=6
        )
        
        # Visual attention
        self.visual_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(text_dim, num_heads=8)
        
        # Projection for cross-modal alignment
        self.image_to_text_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, text_dim)
        
        # Output projection
        self.output_proj = nn.Linear(text_dim, vocab_size)
    
    def forward(self, image_features: torch.Tensor,
                text_tokens: torch.Tensor,
                text_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Args:
            image_features: [B, image_dim]
            text_tokens: [B, seq_len]
            text_mask: [seq_len, seq_len]
        Returns:
            logits: [B, seq_len, vocab_size]
        """
        # Encode image
        img_enc = self.image_encoder(image_features)  # [B, H]
        img_enc = self.image_to_text_proj(img_enc).unsqueeze(0)  # [1, B, D]
        
        # Embed text
        text_emb = self.text_embedding(text_tokens)  # [B, S, D]
        text_emb = text_emb.transpose(0, 1)  # [S, B, D]
        
        # Decode with visual attention
        decoded = self.decoder(
            tgt=text_emb,
            memory=img_enc,
            tgt_mask=text_mask
        )  # [S, B, D]
        
        # Project to vocabulary
        logits = self.output_proj(decoded.transpose(0, 1))  # [B, S, V]
        
        return logits
    
    def compute_alignment_score(self, image_features: torch.Tensor,
                               text_features: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Compute alignment score between image and text"""
        img_enc = F.normalize(self.image_encoder(image_features), dim=-1)
        text_enc = F.normalize(text_features, dim=-1)
        
        return (img_enc * text_enc).sum(dim=-1)


# =============================================================================
# 2328. Semantic Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class SemanticAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns representations based on semantic similarity.
    Uses knowledge graphs or semantic embeddings.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 512, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 semantic_dim: int = 300, hidden_dim: int = 512):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Semantic space projections
        self.mod1_to_semantic = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, semantic_dim)
        )
        
        self.mod2_to_semantic = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, semantic_dim)
        )
        
        # Semantic graph attention
        self.semantic_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            semantic_dim, num_heads=4
        )
        
        # Refinement network
        self.refinement = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(semantic_dim * 2, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, semantic_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, modality1: torch.Tensor, modality2: torch.Tensor,
                semantic_graph: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            modality1: [B, modality1_dim]
            modality2: [B, modality2_dim]
            semantic_graph: [num_concepts, semantic_dim] - optional
        Returns:
            aligned_mod1: [B, semantic_dim]
            aligned_mod2: [B, semantic_dim]
            semantic_loss: scalar
        """
        # Project to semantic space
        sem1 = self.mod1_to_semantic(modality1)  # [B, S]
        sem2 = self.mod2_to_semantic(modality2)  # [B, S]
        
        # If semantic graph provided, align with it
        if semantic_graph is not None:
            sem1 = sem1.unsqueeze(0)  # [1, B, S]
            graph = semantic_graph.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, sem1.shape[1], -1)  # [C, B, S]
            
            # Attend to semantic concepts
            refined_sem1, _ = self.semantic_attention(sem1, graph, graph)
            sem1 = refined_sem1.squeeze(0)
            
            sem2 = sem2.unsqueeze(0)
            refined_sem2, _ = self.semantic_attention(sem2, graph, graph)
            sem2 = refined_sem2.squeeze(0)
        
        # Normalize
        aligned_mod1 = F.normalize(sem1, dim=-1)
        aligned_mod2 = F.normalize(sem2, dim=-1)
        
        # Semantic alignment loss (cosine similarity)
        semantic_loss = 1 - (aligned_mod1 * aligned_mod2).sum(dim=-1).mean()
        
        return aligned_mod1, aligned_mod2, semantic_loss


# =============================================================================
# 2329. Feature Space Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class FeatureSpaceAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns feature spaces of different modalities through adversarial training
    and distribution matching.
    """
    def __init__(self, source_dim: int = 2048, target_dim: int = 768,
                 shared_dim: int = 512):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Feature extractors
        self.source_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(source_dim, shared_dim * 2),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim)
        )
        
        self.target_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(target_dim, shared_dim * 2),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim)
        )
        
        # Domain discriminator for adversarial alignment
        self.discriminator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim // 2, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        # Distribution matcher
        self.distribution_matcher = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, source_features: torch.Tensor,
                target_features: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            source_features: [B, source_dim]
            target_features: [B, target_dim]
        Returns:
            source_aligned: [B, shared_dim]
            target_aligned: [B, shared_dim]
            domain_loss: scalar
        """
        # Encode to shared space
        source_aligned = self.source_encoder(source_features)
        target_aligned = self.target_encoder(target_features)
        
        # Domain discrimination
        source_domain = self.discriminator(source_aligned)
        target_domain = self.discriminator(target_aligned)
        
        # Adversarial loss (want discriminator to fail)
        domain_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy(
            source_domain, 
            torch.ones_like(source_domain)
        ) + F.binary_cross_entropy(
            target_domain,
            torch.zeros_like(target_domain)
        )
        
        return source_aligned, target_aligned, domain_loss
    
    def mmd_loss(self, source: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Maximum Mean Discrepancy for distribution matching"""
        def gaussian_kernel(x, y, sigma=1.0):
            dist = torch.cdist(x, y, p=2)
            return torch.exp(-dist ** 2 / (2 * sigma ** 2))
        
        xx = gaussian_kernel(source, source).mean()
        yy = gaussian_kernel(target, target).mean()
        xy = gaussian_kernel(source, target).mean()
        
        return xx + yy - 2 * xy


# =============================================================================
# 2330. Embedding Space Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class EmbeddingSpaceAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns embeddings from different modalities using geometric transformations
    and metric learning.
    """
    def __init__(self, embed_dim: int = 512, num_modalities: int = 2):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_modalities = num_modalities
        
        # Modality-specific transformations
        self.transformations = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim)
            ) for _ in range(num_modalities)
        ])
        
        # Shared projection
        self.shared_projection = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, embed_dim),
            nn.LayerNorm(embed_dim)
        )
        
        # Metric learning network
        self.metric_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_dim * 2, embed_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(embed_dim, 1)
        )
    
    def forward(self, embeddings: List[torch.Tensor]) -> List[torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            embeddings: List of [B, embed_dim] tensors
        Returns:
            aligned_embeddings: List of [B, embed_dim] tensors
        """
        aligned = []
        
        for i, emb in enumerate(embeddings):
            # Apply modality-specific transformation
            transformed = self.transformations[i](emb)
            
            # Project to shared space
            shared = self.shared_projection(transformed)
            
            # Normalize
            aligned.append(F.normalize(shared, dim=-1))
        
        return aligned
    
    def contrastive_loss(self, aligned_embeddings: List[torch.Tensor],
                        temperature: float = 0.07) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Multi-modal contrastive loss"""
        losses = []
        
        # Pairwise contrastive loss between all modality pairs
        for i in range(len(aligned_
```python
        for i in range(len(aligned_embeddings)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(aligned_embeddings)):
                # Compute similarity matrix
                sim_matrix = aligned_embeddings[i] @ aligned_embeddings[j].t()
                sim_matrix = sim_matrix / temperature
                
                # Labels are diagonal (matching pairs)
                batch_size = sim_matrix.shape[0]
                labels = torch.arange(batch_size, device=sim_matrix.device)
                
                # Symmetric loss
                loss_ij = F.cross_entropy(sim_matrix, labels)
                loss_ji = F.cross_entropy(sim_matrix.t(), labels)
                
                losses.append((loss_ij + loss_ji) / 2)
        
        return sum(losses) / len(losses) if losses else torch.tensor(0.0)
    
    def metric_loss(self, emb1: torch.Tensor, emb2: torch.Tensor,
                   labels: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Metric learning loss for embedding alignment"""
        combined = torch.cat([emb1, emb2], dim=-1)
        distances = self.metric_network(combined).squeeze(-1)
        
        # Binary cross-entropy for same/different pairs
        return F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(distances, labels.float())


# =============================================================================
# 2331. Latent Space Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class LatentSpaceAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns latent representations using VAE-style encoders and shared prior.
    Enables cross-modal generation and translation.
    """
    def __init__(self, input_dim1: int = 2048, input_dim2: int = 768,
                 latent_dim: int = 256, hidden_dim: int = 512):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.latent_dim = latent_dim
        
        # Encoder for modality 1
        self.encoder1_mean = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim1, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        self.encoder1_logvar = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim1, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        # Encoder for modality 2
        self.encoder2_mean = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim2, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        self.encoder2_logvar = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim2, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        # Shared decoder heads
        self.decoder1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim1)
        )
        
        self.decoder2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, input_dim2)
        )
    
    def encode(self, x: torch.Tensor, modality: int = 1) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Encode input to latent distribution"""
        if modality == 1:
            mean = self.encoder1_mean(x)
            logvar = self.encoder1_logvar(x)
        else:
            mean = self.encoder2_mean(x)
            logvar = self.encoder2_logvar(x)
        
        return mean, logvar
    
    def reparameterize(self, mean: torch.Tensor, logvar: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Reparameterization trick"""
        std = torch.exp(0.5 * logvar)
        eps = torch.randn_like(std)
        return mean + eps * std
    
    def decode(self, z: torch.Tensor, modality: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Decode latent to reconstruction"""
        if modality == 1:
            return self.decoder1(z)
        else:
            return self.decoder2(z)
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, input_dim1]
            x2: [B, input_dim2]
        Returns:
            recon_x1, recon_x2, mean1, logvar1, mean2, logvar2, z_shared
        """
        # Encode both modalities
        mean1, logvar1 = self.encode(x1, modality=1)
        mean2, logvar2 = self.encode(x2, modality=2)
        
        # Sample latent codes
        z1 = self.reparameterize(mean1, logvar1)
        z2 = self.reparameterize(mean2, logvar2)
        
        # Shared latent (average)
        z_shared = (z1 + z2) / 2
        
        # Decode
        recon_x1 = self.decode(z_shared, modality=1)
        recon_x2 = self.decode(z_shared, modality=2)
        
        return recon_x1, recon_x2, mean1, logvar1, mean2, logvar2, z_shared
    
    def loss_function(self, recon_x1: torch.Tensor, x1: torch.Tensor,
                     recon_x2: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor,
                     mean1: torch.Tensor, logvar1: torch.Tensor,
                     mean2: torch.Tensor, logvar2: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """VAE loss with alignment"""
        # Reconstruction losses
        recon_loss1 = F.mse_loss(recon_x1, x1, reduction='sum')
        recon_loss2 = F.mse_loss(recon_x2, x2, reduction='sum')
        
        # KL divergences
        kl_loss1 = -0.5 * torch.sum(1 + logvar1 - mean1.pow(2) - logvar1.exp())
        kl_loss2 = -0.5 * torch.sum(1 + logvar2 - mean2.pow(2) - logvar2.exp())
        
        # Alignment loss (latent distributions should match)
        alignment_loss = F.mse_loss(mean1, mean2) + F.mse_loss(logvar1, logvar2)
        
        total_loss = recon_loss1 + recon_loss2 + kl_loss1 + kl_loss2 + alignment_loss
        
        return total_loss / x1.shape[0]


# =============================================================================
# 2332. Cross-Modal Translation Pattern
# =============================================================================

class CrossModalTranslation(nn.Module):
    """
    Translates between modalities using encoder-decoder architecture.
    Supports bidirectional translation with cycle consistency.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 hidden_dim: int = 512, latent_dim: int = 256):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Modality 1 to Modality 2
        self.encoder_1to2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        self.decoder_1to2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, modality2_dim)
        )
        
        # Modality 2 to Modality 1
        self.encoder_2to1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, latent_dim)
        )
        
        self.decoder_2to1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(latent_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, modality1_dim)
        )
        
        # Discriminators for adversarial training
        self.discriminator1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
        
        self.discriminator2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, hidden_dim // 2),
            nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim // 2, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def translate_1to2(self, x1: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Translate from modality 1 to modality 2"""
        latent = self.encoder_1to2(x1)
        x2_pred = self.decoder_1to2(latent)
        return x2_pred
    
    def translate_2to1(self, x2: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Translate from modality 2 to modality 1"""
        latent = self.encoder_2to1(x2)
        x1_pred = self.decoder_2to1(latent)
        return x1_pred
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple:
        """
        Bidirectional translation with cycle consistency.
        
        Args:
            x1: [B, modality1_dim]
            x2: [B, modality2_dim]
        Returns:
            x2_pred, x1_pred, x1_cyclic, x2_cyclic
        """
        # Forward translations
        x2_pred = self.translate_1to2(x1)
        x1_pred = self.translate_2to1(x2)
        
        # Cycle reconstructions
        x1_cyclic = self.translate_2to1(x2_pred)
        x2_cyclic = self.translate_1to2(x1_pred)
        
        return x2_pred, x1_pred, x1_cyclic, x2_cyclic
    
    def translation_loss(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor,
                        x2_pred: torch.Tensor, x1_pred: torch.Tensor,
                        x1_cyclic: torch.Tensor, x2_cyclic: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Combined translation and cycle consistency loss"""
        # Translation loss (if paired data available)
        trans_loss = F.mse_loss(x2_pred, x2) + F.mse_loss(x1_pred, x1)
        
        # Cycle consistency loss
        cycle_loss = F.mse_loss(x1_cyclic, x1) + F.mse_loss(x2_cyclic, x2)
        
        # Adversarial loss
        real_score1 = self.discriminator1(x1)
        fake_score1 = self.discriminator1(x1_pred)
        adv_loss1 = F.binary_cross_entropy(fake_score1, torch.ones_like(fake_score1))
        
        real_score2 = self.discriminator2(x2)
        fake_score2 = self.discriminator2(x2_pred)
        adv_loss2 = F.binary_cross_entropy(fake_score2, torch.ones_like(fake_score2))
        
        return trans_loss + cycle_loss + 0.1 * (adv_loss1 + adv_loss2)


# =============================================================================
# 2333. Modality Bridging Pattern
# =============================================================================

class ModalityBridging(nn.Module):
    """
    Creates a bridge between modalities using intermediate representations.
    Useful when direct alignment is difficult.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 bridge_dim: int = 512, num_bridge_layers: int = 3):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Encoder to bridge
        self.to_bridge1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, bridge_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim * 2, bridge_dim)
        )
        
        self.to_bridge2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, bridge_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim * 2, bridge_dim)
        )
        
        # Bridge transformer
        bridge_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=bridge_dim,
            nhead=8,
            dim_feedforward=bridge_dim * 4
        )
        self.bridge_transformer = nn.TransformerEncoder(
            bridge_layer,
            num_layers=num_bridge_layers
        )
        
        # Decoder from bridge
        self.from_bridge1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim, bridge_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim * 2, modality1_dim)
        )
        
        self.from_bridge2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim, bridge_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(bridge_dim * 2, modality2_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x1: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
                x2: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, modality1_dim] - optional
            x2: [B, modality2_dim] - optional
        Returns:
            bridge_repr, recon_x1, recon_x2
        """
        bridge_reprs = []
        
        # Encode to bridge
        if x1 is not None:
            bridge1 = self.to_bridge1(x1)
            bridge_reprs.append(bridge1.unsqueeze(0))
        
        if x2 is not None:
            bridge2 = self.to_bridge2(x2)
            bridge_reprs.append(bridge2.unsqueeze(0))
        
        # Concatenate and process through bridge
        if bridge_reprs:
            bridge_combined = torch.cat(bridge_reprs, dim=0)  # [N, B, D]
            bridge_processed = self.bridge_transformer(bridge_combined)
            
            # Average pooling across modalities
            bridge_repr = bridge_processed.mean(dim=0)  # [B, D]
            
            # Decode back to original modalities
            recon_x1 = self.from_bridge1(bridge_repr
```python
            recon_x1 = self.from_bridge1(bridge_repr) if x1 is not None else None
            recon_x2 = self.from_bridge2(bridge_repr) if x2 is not None else None
            
            return bridge_repr, recon_x1, recon_x2
        else:
            raise ValueError("At least one modality must be provided")
    
    def bridge_loss(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor,
                   recon_x1: torch.Tensor, recon_x2: torch.Tensor,
                   bridge_repr: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Loss for modality bridging"""
        # Reconstruction losses
        loss_recon1 = F.mse_loss(recon_x1, x1)
        loss_recon2 = F.mse_loss(recon_x2, x2)
        
        # Bridge consistency (both modalities should produce similar bridge)
        bridge1 = self.to_bridge1(x1)
        bridge2 = self.to_bridge2(x2)
        loss_consistency = F.mse_loss(bridge1, bridge2)
        
        return loss_recon1 + loss_recon2 + 0.5 * loss_consistency


# =============================================================================
# 2334. Shared Representation Learning Pattern
# =============================================================================

class SharedRepresentationLearning(nn.Module):
    """
    Learns shared representations across modalities using multi-task learning.
    Encourages modality-invariant features.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality_dims: List[int], shared_dim: int = 512,
                 num_tasks: int = 3):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_modalities = len(modality_dims)
        self.num_tasks = num_tasks
        
        # Modality-specific encoders
        self.modality_encoders = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(dim, shared_dim * 2),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim * 2),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.2),
                nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(shared_dim)
            ) for dim in modality_dims
        ])
        
        # Shared encoder (processes all modality encodings)
        self.shared_encoder = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.LayerNorm(shared_dim)
        )
        
        # Task-specific heads
        self.task_heads = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim // 2),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1),
                nn.Linear(shared_dim // 2, 128)
            ) for _ in range(num_tasks)
        ])
        
        # Modality discriminator (for adversarial invariance)
        self.modality_discriminator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim // 2, self.num_modalities),
            nn.Softmax(dim=-1)
        )
    
    def forward(self, modality_inputs: List[torch.Tensor],
                task_id: Optional[int] = None) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            modality_inputs: List of [B, modality_dim] tensors
            task_id: Optional task identifier
        Returns:
            shared_reprs: List of [B, shared_dim]
            task_outputs: List of task predictions
            modality_preds: [B, num_modalities]
        """
        shared_reprs = []
        
        # Encode each modality
        for i, (encoder, x) in enumerate(zip(self.modality_encoders, modality_inputs)):
            if x is not None:
                modality_repr = encoder(x)
                shared_repr = self.shared_encoder(modality_repr)
                shared_reprs.append(shared_repr)
        
        # Aggregate shared representations
        if len(shared_reprs) > 1:
            aggregated = torch.stack(shared_reprs).mean(dim=0)
        else:
            aggregated = shared_reprs[0]
        
        # Task-specific predictions
        task_outputs = []
        if task_id is not None:
            task_output = self.task_heads[task_id](aggregated)
            task_outputs.append(task_output)
        else:
            for head in self.task_heads:
                task_outputs.append(head(aggregated))
        
        # Modality discrimination (for adversarial training)
        modality_preds = self.modality_discriminator(aggregated)
        
        return shared_reprs, task_outputs, modality_preds
    
    def adversarial_loss(self, modality_preds: torch.Tensor,
                        true_modalities: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Adversarial loss for modality-invariant features"""
        # Want to maximize confusion (uniform distribution)
        uniform_target = torch.ones_like(modality_preds) / self.num_modalities
        return F.kl_div(modality_preds.log(), uniform_target, reduction='batchmean')


# =============================================================================
# 2335. Joint Embedding Pattern
# =============================================================================

class JointEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """
    Creates joint embeddings by combining multiple modalities.
    Uses attention-based fusion.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality_dims: List[int], joint_dim: int = 512,
                 num_heads: int = 8):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_modalities = len(modality_dims)
        
        # Project each modality to joint dimension
        self.modality_projections = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(dim, joint_dim),
                nn.LayerNorm(joint_dim)
            ) for dim in modality_dims
        ])
        
        # Multi-head attention for fusion
        self.fusion_attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=joint_dim,
            num_heads=num_heads
        )
        
        # Gating mechanism for modality importance
        self.gate_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(joint_dim * self.num_modalities, joint_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(joint_dim, self.num_modalities),
            nn.Softmax(dim=-1)
        )
        
        # Final projection
        self.output_projection = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(joint_dim, joint_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.LayerNorm(joint_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, modality_inputs: List[torch.Tensor],
                modality_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            modality_inputs: List of [B, modality_dim] tensors
            modality_mask: [B, num_modalities] - binary mask for available modalities
        Returns:
            joint_embedding: [B, joint_dim]
            attention_weights: [B, num_modalities, num_modalities]
        """
        batch_size = modality_inputs[0].shape[0]
        
        # Project all modalities
        projected = []
        for i, (proj, x) in enumerate(zip(self.modality_projections, modality_inputs)):
            if x is not None:
                projected.append(proj(x))
            else:
                # Use zero tensor for missing modality
                projected.append(torch.zeros(batch_size, self.output_projection[-1].normalized_shape[0],
                                            device=modality_inputs[0].device))
        
        # Stack modalities: [num_modalities, batch, joint_dim]
        stacked = torch.stack(projected, dim=0)
        
        # Apply self-attention across modalities
        attended, attention_weights = self.fusion_attention(
            stacked, stacked, stacked
        )  # [M, B, D], [B, M, M]
        
        # Compute modality gates
        concatenated = torch.cat(projected, dim=-1)  # [B, M*D]
        gates = self.gate_network(concatenated)  # [B, M]
        
        # Weighted combination
        gates = gates.unsqueeze(-1)  # [B, M, 1]
        weighted = (attended.transpose(0, 1) * gates).sum(dim=1)  # [B, D]
        
        # Final projection
        joint_embedding = self.output_projection(weighted)
        
        return joint_embedding, attention_weights
    
    def reconstruction_loss(self, joint_embedding: torch.Tensor,
                          original_inputs: List[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Reconstruct individual modalities from joint embedding"""
        total_loss = 0
        
        for i, (proj, x) in enumerate(zip(self.modality_projections, original_inputs)):
            if x is not None:
                # Inverse projection (approximate)
                reconstructed = proj[0](joint_embedding)  # Use first layer in reverse
                total_loss += F.mse_loss(reconstructed, x)
        
        return total_loss / len(original_inputs)


# =============================================================================
# 2336. Coordinated Representation Pattern
# =============================================================================

class CoordinatedRepresentation(nn.Module):
    """
    Coordinates representations across modalities using synchronized learning.
    Maintains both private and shared components.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 shared_dim: int = 256, private_dim: int = 128):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Shared encoders
        self.shared_encoder1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, shared_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim)
        )
        
        self.shared_encoder2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, shared_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim)
        )
        
        # Private encoders (modality-specific features)
        self.private_encoder1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, private_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(private_dim * 2, private_dim)
        )
        
        self.private_encoder2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, private_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(private_dim * 2, private_dim)
        )
        
        # Coordination network
        self.coordination_net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim * 2, shared_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(shared_dim, shared_dim)
        )
        
        # Reconstruction decoders
        self.decoder1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim + private_dim, modality1_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim * 2, modality1_dim)
        )
        
        self.decoder2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(shared_dim + private_dim, modality2_dim * 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim * 2, modality2_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, modality1_dim]
            x2: [B, modality2_dim]
        Returns:
            shared1, shared2, private1, private2, coordinated, recon1, recon2
        """
        # Extract shared representations
        shared1 = self.shared_encoder1(x1)
        shared2 = self.shared_encoder2(x2)
        
        # Extract private representations
        private1 = self.private_encoder1(x1)
        private2 = self.private_encoder2(x2)
        
        # Coordinate shared representations
        combined_shared = torch.cat([shared1, shared2], dim=-1)
        coordinated = self.coordination_net(combined_shared)
        
        # Reconstruct using shared + private
        combined1 = torch.cat([coordinated, private1], dim=-1)
        combined2 = torch.cat([coordinated, private2], dim=-1)
        
        recon1 = self.decoder1(combined1)
        recon2 = self.decoder2(combined2)
        
        return shared1, shared2, private1, private2, coordinated, recon1, recon2
    
    def coordination_loss(self, shared1: torch.Tensor, shared2: torch.Tensor,
                         private1: torch.Tensor, private2: torch.Tensor,
                         x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor,
                         recon1: torch.Tensor, recon2: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Multi-objective loss:
        1. Shared representations should be similar
        2. Private representations should be orthogonal to shared
        3. Reconstruction should be accurate
        """
        # Shared similarity loss
        shared_loss = F.mse_loss(shared1, shared2)
        
        # Orthogonality loss (private should not correlate with shared)
        ortho_loss1 = torch.abs((private1 * shared1).sum(dim=-1)).mean()
        ortho_loss2 = torch.abs((private2 * shared2).sum(dim=-1)).mean()
        
        # Reconstruction loss
        recon_loss = F.mse_loss(recon1, x1) + F.mse_loss(recon2, x2)
        
        return shared_loss + 0.1 * (ortho_loss1 + ortho_loss2) + recon_loss


# =============================================================================
# 2337. Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) Pattern
# =============================================================================

class CCAAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Deep Canonical Correlation Analysis for finding correlated projections.
    Maximizes correlation between modality representations.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 output_dim: int = 512, hidden_dim: int = 1024):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        
        # Deep networks for each modality
        self.network1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality1_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.Sigmoid(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.Sigmoid(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        )
        
        self.network2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(modality2_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.Sigmoid(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.Sigmoid(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
```python
        )
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, modality1_dim]
            x2: [B, modality2_dim]
        Returns:
            h1: [B, output_dim]
            h2: [B, output_dim]
        """
        h1 = self.network1(x1)
        h2 = self.network2(x2)
        
        return h1, h2
    
    def cca_loss(self, h1: torch.Tensor, h2: torch.Tensor, 
                 reg_param: float = 1e-4) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute CCA loss (negative correlation).
        
        Args:
            h1: [B, output_dim]
            h2: [B, output_dim]
            reg_param: regularization parameter
        Returns:
            loss: scalar
        """
        batch_size = h1.shape[0]
        
        # Center the representations
        h1_mean = h1.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        h2_mean = h2.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        
        h1_centered = h1 - h1_mean
        h2_centered = h2 - h2_mean
        
        # Compute covariance matrices
        cov_h1h1 = (h1_centered.t() @ h1_centered) / (batch_size - 1)
        cov_h2h2 = (h2_centered.t() @ h2_centered) / (batch_size - 1)
        cov_h1h2 = (h1_centered.t() @ h2_centered) / (batch_size - 1)
        
        # Add regularization
        cov_h1h1 = cov_h1h1 + reg_param * torch.eye(self.output_dim, device=h1.device)
        cov_h2h2 = cov_h2h2 + reg_param * torch.eye(self.output_dim, device=h2.device)
        
        # Compute correlation (using trace of cross-covariance)
        # CCA objective: maximize trace(cov_h1h2.T @ inv(cov_h1h1) @ cov_h1h2 @ inv(cov_h2h2))
        # Simplified: maximize trace(cov_h1h2.T @ cov_h1h2) with normalized covariances
        
        correlation = torch.trace(cov_h1h2.t() @ cov_h1h2)
        
        # Normalize by variances
        norm1 = torch.sqrt(torch.trace(cov_h1h1))
        norm2 = torch.sqrt(torch.trace(cov_h2h2))
        
        normalized_correlation = correlation / (norm1 * norm2 + 1e-8)
        
        # Return negative correlation (for minimization)
        return -normalized_correlation


# =============================================================================
# 2338. Deep CCA Pattern
# =============================================================================

class DeepCCA(nn.Module):
    """
    Enhanced Deep CCA with non-linear transformations and multiple layers.
    Uses gradient-based optimization of CCA objective.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 layer_sizes1: List[int] = [1024, 512, 256],
                 layer_sizes2: List[int] = [512, 256, 256],
                 output_dim: int = 256):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        
        # Build deep network for modality 1
        layers1 = []
        prev_dim = modality1_dim
        for hidden_dim in layer_sizes1:
            layers1.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1)
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        layers1.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, output_dim))
        self.network1 = nn.Sequential(*layers1)
        
        # Build deep network for modality 2
        layers2 = []
        prev_dim = modality2_dim
        for hidden_dim in layer_sizes2:
            layers2.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1)
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        layers2.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, output_dim))
        self.network2 = nn.Sequential(*layers2)
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, modality1_dim]
            x2: [B, modality2_dim]
        Returns:
            h1: [B, output_dim]
            h2: [B, output_dim]
        """
        h1 = self.network1(x1)
        h2 = self.network2(x2)
        
        return h1, h2
    
    def deep_cca_loss(self, h1: torch.Tensor, h2: torch.Tensor,
                     reg_param: float = 1e-3, use_all_singular_values: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Deep CCA loss using SVD-based computation.
        
        Args:
            h1: [B, output_dim]
            h2: [B, output_dim]
            reg_param: regularization parameter
            use_all_singular_values: if True, use sum of all singular values
        Returns:
            loss: scalar
        """
        batch_size = h1.shape[0]
        
        # Remove mean
        h1_mean = h1.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        h2_mean = h2.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
        
        h1_bar = h1 - h1_mean
        h2_bar = h2 - h2_mean
        
        # Compute covariance matrices
        sigma11 = (h1_bar.t() @ h1_bar) / (batch_size - 1) + reg_param * torch.eye(
            self.output_dim, device=h1.device
        )
        sigma22 = (h2_bar.t() @ h2_bar) / (batch_size - 1) + reg_param * torch.eye(
            self.output_dim, device=h2.device
        )
        sigma12 = (h1_bar.t() @ h2_bar) / (batch_size - 1)
        
        # Compute the matrix for SVD: inv(sigma11^0.5) @ sigma12 @ inv(sigma22^0.5)
        # Using Cholesky decomposition for stability
        try:
            L1 = torch.linalg.cholesky(sigma11)
            L2 = torch.linalg.cholesky(sigma22)
        except:
            # Fallback to eigenvalue decomposition if Cholesky fails
            L1 = self._matrix_sqrt(sigma11)
            L2 = self._matrix_sqrt(sigma22)
        
        # Solve linear systems
        T = torch.linalg.solve(L1, sigma12)
        T = torch.linalg.solve(L2.t(), T.t()).t()
        
        # Compute SVD
        U, S, V = torch.svd(T)
        
        # CCA objective: maximize sum of correlations (singular values)
        if use_all_singular_values:
            corr = S.sum()
        else:
            # Use top-k singular values
            corr = S[:min(10, len(S))].sum()
        
        return -corr
    
    def _matrix_sqrt(self, matrix: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Compute matrix square root using eigenvalue decomposition"""
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = torch.linalg.eigh(matrix)
        eigenvalues = torch.clamp(eigenvalues, min=1e-8)
        return eigenvectors @ torch.diag(torch.sqrt(eigenvalues)) @ eigenvectors.t()


# =============================================================================
# 2339. Multimodal Bottleneck Pattern
# =============================================================================

class MultimodalBottleneck(nn.Module):
    """
    Forces information through a bottleneck to learn compact multimodal representations.
    Encourages fusion of complementary information.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality_dims: List[int], bottleneck_dim: int = 128,
                 hidden_dim: int = 512, output_dim: int = 256):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.num_modalities = len(modality_dims)
        
        # Encoders to bottleneck
        self.encoders = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.2),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, bottleneck_dim),
                nn.Tanh()  # Bounded activation for bottleneck
            ) for dim in modality_dims
        ])
        
        # Fusion network (processes concatenated bottlenecks)
        self.fusion = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bottleneck_dim * self.num_modalities, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        )
        
        # Decoders from bottleneck (for reconstruction)
        self.decoders = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(bottleneck_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.2),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, dim)
            ) for dim in modality_dims
        ])
        
        # Information bottleneck regularizer
        self.ib_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(bottleneck_dim, bottleneck_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(bottleneck_dim // 2, bottleneck_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, modality_inputs: List[torch.Tensor]) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            modality_inputs: List of [B, modality_dim] tensors
        Returns:
            bottlenecks: List of [B, bottleneck_dim]
            fused_output: [B, output_dim]
            reconstructions: List of [B, modality_dim]
        """
        # Encode each modality to bottleneck
        bottlenecks = []
        for encoder, x in zip(self.encoders, modality_inputs):
            bottleneck = encoder(x)
            bottlenecks.append(bottleneck)
        
        # Concatenate and fuse
        concatenated = torch.cat(bottlenecks, dim=-1)
        fused_output = self.fusion(concatenated)
        
        # Reconstruct from individual bottlenecks
        reconstructions = []
        for decoder, bottleneck in zip(self.decoders, bottlenecks):
            recon = decoder(bottleneck)
            reconstructions.append(recon)
        
        return bottlenecks, fused_output, reconstructions
    
    def bottleneck_loss(self, modality_inputs: List[torch.Tensor],
                       bottlenecks: List[torch.Tensor],
                       reconstructions: List[torch.Tensor],
                       beta: float = 0.01) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Information bottleneck loss with reconstruction.
        
        Args:
            modality_inputs: original inputs
            bottlenecks: bottleneck representations
            reconstructions: reconstructed inputs
            beta: weight for information constraint
        Returns:
            loss: scalar
        """
        # Reconstruction loss
        recon_loss = sum(
            F.mse_loss(recon, orig) 
            for recon, orig in zip(reconstructions, modality_inputs)
        ) / len(modality_inputs)
        
        # Information bottleneck regularization
        # Encourage minimal sufficient statistics
        ib_loss = 0
        for bottleneck in bottlenecks:
            # Measure information content (variance)
            variance = bottleneck.var(dim=0).mean()
            ib_loss += variance
        
        ib_loss = ib_loss / len(bottlenecks)
        
        return recon_loss + beta * ib_loss
    
    def complementarity_loss(self, bottlenecks: List[torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Encourage bottlenecks to capture complementary information.
        Minimize correlation between different modality bottlenecks.
        """
        total_corr = 0
        count = 0
        
        for i in range(len(bottlenecks)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(bottlenecks)):
                # Compute correlation
                b1 = bottlenecks[i] - bottlenecks[i].mean(dim=0)
                b2 = bottlenecks[j] - bottlenecks[j].mean(dim=0)
                
                corr = (b1 * b2).sum(dim=0).abs().mean()
                total_corr += corr
                count += 1
        
        return total_corr / count if count > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0)


# =============================================================================
# 2340. Cross-Modal Attention Alignment Pattern
# =============================================================================

class CrossModalAttentionAlignment(nn.Module):
    """
    Aligns modalities using cross-attention mechanisms.
    Each modality attends to others for alignment.
    """
    def __init__(self, modality1_dim: int = 2048, modality2_dim: int = 768,
                 hidden_dim: int = 512, num_heads: int = 8, num_layers: int = 3):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Project modalities to same dimension
        self.proj1 = nn.Linear(modality1_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.proj2 = nn.Linear(modality2_dim, hidden_dim)
        
        # Cross-attention layers
        self.cross_attention_1to2 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.MultiheadAttention(hidden_dim, num_heads, batch_first=True)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.cross_attention_2to1 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.MultiheadAttention(hidden_dim, num_heads, batch_first=True)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        # Feed-forward networks
        self.ffn1 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim * 4),
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 4, hidden_dim)
            ) for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        self.ffn2 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim * 4),
                
```python
                nn.ReLU(),
                nn.Dropout(0.1),
                nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 4, hidden_dim)
            ) for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        
        # Layer normalization
        self.layer_norms1 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim) for _ in range(num_layers * 2)
        ])
        
        self.layer_norms2 = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim) for _ in range(num_layers * 2)
        ])
        
        # Alignment scorer
        self.alignment_scorer = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 2, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 1)
        )
        
        # Output projections
        self.output_proj1 = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.output_proj2 = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor,
                return_attention: bool = False) -> Tuple:
        """
        Args:
            x1: [B, seq_len1, modality1_dim] or [B, modality1_dim]
            x2: [B, seq_len2, modality2_dim] or [B, modality2_dim]
            return_attention: whether to return attention weights
        Returns:
            aligned1: [B, hidden_dim]
            aligned2: [B, hidden_dim]
            alignment_score: [B]
            attention_weights: dict (optional)
        """
        # Handle single vectors by adding sequence dimension
        if x1.dim() == 2:
            x1 = x1.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1, D]
        if x2.dim() == 2:
            x2 = x2.unsqueeze(1)  # [B, 1, D]
        
        # Project to hidden dimension
        h1 = self.proj1(x1)  # [B, S1, H]
        h2 = self.proj2(x2)  # [B, S2, H]
        
        attention_weights = {'1to2': [], '2to1': []}
        
        # Cross-attention layers
        for layer_idx in range(len(self.cross_attention_1to2)):
            # h1 attends to h2
            attn_output_1, attn_weights_1 = self.cross_attention_1to2[layer_idx](
                h1, h2, h2
            )
            h1 = self.layer_norms1[layer_idx * 2](h1 + attn_output_1)
            
            # Feed-forward
            ffn_output_1 = self.ffn1[layer_idx](h1)
            h1 = self.layer_norms1[layer_idx * 2 + 1](h1 + ffn_output_1)
            
            # h2 attends to h1
            attn_output_2, attn_weights_2 = self.cross_attention_2to1[layer_idx](
                h2, h1, h1
            )
            h2 = self.layer_norms2[layer_idx * 2](h2 + attn_output_2)
            
            # Feed-forward
            ffn_output_2 = self.ffn2[layer_idx](h2)
            h2 = self.layer_norms2[layer_idx * 2 + 1](h2 + ffn_output_2)
            
            if return_attention:
                attention_weights['1to2'].append(attn_weights_1)
                attention_weights['2to1'].append(attn_weights_2)
        
        # Pool sequences
        aligned1 = h1.mean(dim=1)  # [B, H]
        aligned2 = h2.mean(dim=1)  # [B, H]
        
        # Final output projection
        aligned1 = self.output_proj1(aligned1)
        aligned2 = self.output_proj2(aligned2)
        
        # Compute alignment score
        combined = torch.cat([aligned1, aligned2], dim=-1)
        alignment_score = self.alignment_scorer(combined).squeeze(-1)
        
        if return_attention:
            return aligned1, aligned2, alignment_score, attention_weights
        else:
            return aligned1, aligned2, alignment_score
    
    def alignment_loss(self, aligned1: torch.Tensor, aligned2: torch.Tensor,
                      alignment_score: torch.Tensor,
                      labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute alignment loss.
        
        Args:
            aligned1: [B, hidden_dim]
            aligned2: [B, hidden_dim]
            alignment_score: [B]
            labels: [B] - binary labels for matching pairs (optional)
        Returns:
            loss: scalar
        """
        # Cosine similarity loss
        cosine_sim = F.cosine_similarity(aligned1, aligned2, dim=-1)
        
        if labels is not None:
            # Supervised alignment
            target_sim = labels.float() * 2 - 1  # Convert {0,1} to {-1,1}
            similarity_loss = F.mse_loss(cosine_sim, target_sim)
            
            # Binary classification loss for alignment score
            score_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
                alignment_score, labels.float()
            )
            
            return similarity_loss + score_loss
        else:
            # Unsupervised: maximize similarity for all pairs
            return -cosine_sim.mean()
    
    def attention_diversity_loss(self, attention_weights: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Encourage diverse attention patterns across layers.
        """
        diversity_loss = 0
        count = 0
        
        for direction in ['1to2', '2to1']:
            weights_list = attention_weights[direction]
            for i in range(len(weights_list)):
                for j in range(i + 1, len(weights_list)):
                    # Compute similarity between attention patterns
                    w1 = weights_list[i].mean(dim=1)  # Average over heads
                    w2 = weights_list[j].mean(dim=1)
                    
                    # Minimize correlation between layers
                    correlation = (w1 * w2).sum(dim=-1).mean()
                    diversity_loss += correlation
                    count += 1
        
        return diversity_loss / count if count > 0 else torch.tensor(0.0)

# Training Example
# =============================================================================

class MultimodalTrainer:
    """
    Example trainer for multimodal alignment patterns.
    Demonstrates how to train these models in practice.
    """
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, learning_rate: float = 1e-4):
        self.model = model
        self.optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)
        self.scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(
            self.optimizer, T_max=100
        )
    
    def train_step_clip(self, image_features: torch.Tensor,
                       text_features: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Training step for CLIP-style model"""
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        logits_img, logits_txt = self.model(image_features, text_features)
        loss = self.model.contrastive_loss(logits_img, logits_txt)
        
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(self.model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)
        self.optimizer.step()
        
        return loss.item()
    
    def train_step_vae(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Training step for VAE-based alignment"""
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        recon1, recon2, mean1, logvar1, mean2, logvar2, z_shared = self.model(x1, x2)
        loss = self.model.loss_function(
            recon1, x1, recon2, x2, mean1, logvar1, mean2, logvar2
        )
        
        loss.backward()
        self.optimizer.step()
        
        return loss.item()
    
    def train_step_translation(self, x1: torch.Tensor, x2: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
        """Training step for cross-modal translation"""
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        x2_pred, x1_pred, x1_cyc, x2_cyc = self.model(x1, x2)
        loss = self.model.translation_loss(x1, x2, x2_pred, x1_pred, x1_cyc, x2_cyc)
        
        loss.backward()
        self.optimizer.step()
        
        return {
            'total_loss': loss.item(),
            'translation_quality': F.mse_loss(x2_pred, x2).item()
        }
    
    def evaluate(self, val_loader: DataLoader, metric_fn) -> float:
        """Evaluation loop"""
        self.model.eval()
        total_metric = 0
        count = 0
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for batch in val_loader:
                metric = metric_fn(self.model, batch)
                total_metric += metric
                count += 1
        
        self.model.train()
        return total_metric / count if count > 0 else 0


# =============================================================================
# Utility Functions
# =============================================================================

def compute_alignment_metrics(embeddings1: torch.Tensor,
                              embeddings2: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
    """
    Compute various alignment metrics between two sets of embeddings.
    
    Args:
        embeddings1: [N, D]
        embeddings2: [N, D]
    Returns:
        metrics: dictionary of alignment metrics
    """
    # Normalize embeddings
    emb1_norm = F.normalize(embeddings1, dim=-1)
    emb2_norm = F.normalize(embeddings2, dim=-1)
    
    # Cosine similarity
    cosine_sim = (emb1_norm * emb2_norm).sum(dim=-1).mean()
    
    # L2 distance
    l2_dist = torch.norm(embeddings1 - embeddings2, p=2, dim=-1).mean()
    
    # Correlation
    emb1_centered = embeddings1 - embeddings1.mean(dim=0)
    emb2_centered = embeddings2 - embeddings2.mean(dim=0)
    correlation = (emb1_centered * emb2_centered).sum() / (
        torch.norm(emb1_centered) * torch.norm(emb2_centered)
    )
    
    # Retrieval accuracy (top-1)
    similarity_matrix = emb1_norm @ emb2_norm.t()
    top1_indices = similarity_matrix.argmax(dim=-1)
    retrieval_acc = (top1_indices == torch.arange(len(embeddings1))).float().mean()
    
    return {
        'cosine_similarity': cosine_sim.item(),
        'l2_distance': l2_dist.item(),
        'correlation': correlation.item(),
        'retrieval_accuracy': retrieval_acc.item()
    }


def visualize_attention_weights(attention_weights: torch.Tensor,
                                source_labels: List[str] = None,
                                target_labels: List[str] = None):
    """
    Visualize attention weights (requires matplotlib).
    
    Args:
        attention_weights: [seq_len_source, seq_len_target]
        source_labels: labels for source sequence
        target_labels: labels for target sequence
    """
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        import seaborn as sns
        
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
        sns.heatmap(
            attention_weights.detach().cpu().numpy(),
            xticklabels=target_labels if target_labels else [],
            yticklabels=source_labels if source_labels else [],
            cmap='viridis',
            cbar=True
        )
        plt.title('Cross-Modal Attention Weights')
        plt.xlabel('Target Modality')
        plt.ylabel('Source Modality')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
    except ImportError:
        print("Matplotlib not available for visualization")


def create_synthetic_multimodal_dataset(num_samples: int = 1000,
                                       image_dim: int = 2048,
                                       text_dim: int = 768,
                                       num_classes: int = 10) -> dict:
    """
    Create synthetic multimodal dataset for testing.
    
    Args:
        num_samples: number of samples to generate
        image_dim: dimension of image features
        text_dim: dimension of text features
        num_classes: number of semantic classes
    Returns:
        dataset: dictionary containing synthetic data
    """
    # Generate class-conditional data
    labels = torch.randint(0, num_classes, (num_samples,))
    
    # Image features with class structure
    image_features = torch.randn(num_samples, image_dim)
    for c in range(num_classes):
        mask = labels == c
        image_features[mask] += torch.randn(1, image_dim) * 2
    
    # Text features with class structure (correlated with images)
    text_features = torch.randn(num_samples, text_dim)
    for c in range(num_classes):
        mask = labels == c
        # Add same offset to create correlation
        text_features[mask] += torch.randn(1, text_dim) * 2
    
    # Add some noise to make it realistic
    image_features += torch.randn_like(image_features) * 0.1
    text_features += torch.randn_like(text_features) * 0.1
    
    return {
        'image_features': image_features,
        'text_features': text_features,
        'labels': labels,
        'num_classes': num_classes
    }


class MultimodalDataset(Dataset):
    """
    PyTorch Dataset for multimodal data.
    """
    def __init__(self, image_features: torch.Tensor,
                 text_features: torch.Tensor,
                 labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None):
        self.image_features = image_features
        self.text_features = text_features
        self.labels = labels
    
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.image_features)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> dict:
        item = {
            'image': self.image_features[idx],
            'text': self.text_features[idx]
        }
        
        if self.labels is not None:
            item['label'] = self.labels[idx]
        
        return item

# Complete Training Example
# =============================================================================

def complete_training_example():
    """
    Complete end-to-end training example using CLIP pattern.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("Complete Training Example: CLIP Pattern")
    print("=" * 70 + "\n")
    
    # Create synthetic dataset
    print("Creating synthetic dataset...")
    data = create_synthetic_multimodal_dataset(num_samples=1000)
    
    # Split into train/val
    train_size = int(0.8 * len(data['image_features']))
    train_dataset = MultimodalDataset(
        data['image_features'][:train_size],
        data['text_features'][:train_size],
        data['labels'][:train_size]
    )
    val_dataset = MultimodalDataset(
        data['image_features'][train_size:],
        data['text_features'][train_size:],
        data['labels'][train_size:]
    )
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=32, shuffle=False)
    
    # Initialize model and trainer
    print("Initializing CLIP model...")
    model = CLIPModel(image_dim=2048, text_dim=768, embed_dim=512)
    trainer = MultimodalTrainer(model, learning_rate=1e-4)
    
    # Training loop
    print("\nTraining for 5 epochs...\n")
    num_epochs = 5
    
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        epoch_loss = 0
        num_batches = 0
        
        for batch in train_loader:
            loss = trainer.train_step_clip(batch['image'], batch['text'])
            epoch_loss += loss
            num_batches += 1
        
        avg_loss = epoch_loss / num_batches
        
        # Compute validation metrics
        val_metrics = []
        for batch in val_loader:
            with torch.no_grad():
                img_emb = model.image_projection(batch['image'])
                txt_emb = model.text_projection(batch['text'])
                metrics = compute_alignment_metrics(img_emb, txt_emb)
                val_metrics.append(metrics)
        
        # Average validation metrics
        avg_metrics = {
            k: np.mean([m[k] for m in val_metrics])
            for k in val_metrics[0].keys()
        }
        
        print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}/{num_epochs}")
        print(f"  Train Loss: {avg_loss:.4f}")
        print(f"  Val Cosine Similarity: {avg_metrics['cosine_similarity']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Val Retrieval Accuracy: {avg_metrics['retrieval_accuracy']:.4f}")
        print()
        
        trainer.scheduler.step()
    
    print("Training completed!")
    print("=" * 70 + "\n")

def demonstrate_cross_modal_retrieval():
    """
    Demonstrate cross-modal retrieval capabilities.
    """
    print("Demonstration: Cross-Modal Retrieval")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    # Create model
    retrieval_model = CrossModalRetrieval(image_dim=2048, text_dim=768, embed_dim=512)
    
    # Generate sample data with known correspondences
    num_items = 50
    image_features = torch.randn(num_items, 2048)
    text_features = torch.randn(num_items, 768)
    
    # Encode to shared space
    image_embeddings = retrieval_model(image_features=image_features)
    text_embeddings = retrieval_model(text_features=text_features)
    
    # Perform text-to-image retrieval
    query_idx = 0
    query_text_emb = text_embeddings[query_idx:query_idx+1]
    
    indices, similarities = retrieval_model.retrieve(
        query_text_emb, image_embeddings, top_k=5
    )
    
    print(f"\nText Query Index: {query_idx}")
    print(f"Top-5 Retrieved Image Indices: {indices[0].tolist()}")
    print(f"Similarity Scores: {similarities[0].tolist()}")
    
    # Compute retrieval metrics
    correct_retrievals = (indices[0] == query_idx).sum().item()
    print(f"Correct in Top-5: {correct_retrievals > 0}")
    
    # Image-to-text retrieval
    query_image_emb = image_embeddings[query_idx:query_idx+1]
    indices, similarities = retrieval_model.retrieve(
        query_image_emb, text_embeddings, top_k=5
    )
    
    print(f"\nImage Query Index: {query_idx}")
    print(f"Top-5 Retrieved Text Indices: {indices[0].tolist()}")
    print(f"Similarity Scores: {similarities[0].tolist()}\n")


def demonstrate_multimodal_fusion():
    """
    Demonstrate multimodal fusion with different patterns.
    """
    print("Demonstration: Multimodal Fusion Strategies")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    batch_size = 16
    modality_dims = [2048, 768, 512]  # Image, Text, Audio
    
    # Generate sample data
    modality_inputs = [
        torch.randn(batch_size, dim) for dim in modality_dims
    ]
    
    # 1. Joint Embedding Fusion
    print("\n1. Joint Embedding Fusion:")
    joint_model = JointEmbedding(modality_dims, joint_dim=512)
    joint_emb, attn_weights = joint_model(modality_inputs)
    print(f"   Joint embedding shape: {joint_emb.shape}")
    print(f"   Attention weights shape: {attn_weights.shape}")
    
    # Analyze attention patterns
    avg_attention = attn_weights.mean(dim=0)
    print(f"   Average attention from each modality:")
    for i in range(len(modality_dims)):
        print(f"     Modality {i}: {avg_attention[i].tolist()}")
    
    # 2. Bottleneck Fusion
    print("\n2. Multimodal Bottleneck Fusion:")
    bottleneck_model = MultimodalBottleneck(modality_dims, bottleneck_dim=128)
    bottlenecks, fused, reconstructions = bottleneck_model(modality_inputs)
    print(f"   Bottleneck dimensions: {[b.shape for b in bottlenecks]}")
    print(f"   Fused output shape: {fused.shape}")
    
    # Compute complementarity
    comp_loss = bottleneck_model.complementarity_loss(bottlenecks)
    print(f"   Complementarity score: {comp_loss.item():.4f}")
    
    # 3. Shared Representation Fusion
    print("\n3. Shared Representation Learning:")
    shared_model = SharedRepresentationLearning(modality_dims, shared_dim=512)
    shared_reprs, task_outputs, mod_preds = shared_model(modality_inputs)
    print(f"   Shared representations: {len(shared_reprs)} modalities")
    print(f"   Task outputs: {len(task_outputs)} tasks")
    
    # Check modality invariance
    mod_entropy = -(mod_preds * torch.log(mod_preds + 1e-8)).sum(dim=-1).mean()
    print(f"   Modality prediction entropy: {mod_entropy.item():.4f}")
    print(f"   (Higher = more modality-invariant)\n")


def demonstrate_alignment_visualization():
    """
    Demonstrate alignment quality visualization.
    """
    print("Demonstration: Alignment Quality Analysis")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    # Create aligned and misaligned pairs
    batch_size = 100
    embed_dim = 512
    
    # Well-aligned pairs
    base_embeddings = torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim)
    aligned_emb1 = base_embeddings + torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim) * 0.1
    aligned_emb2 = base_embeddings + torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim) * 0.1
    
    # Misaligned pairs
    misaligned_emb1 = torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim)
    misaligned_emb2 = torch.randn(batch_size, embed_dim)
    
    # Compute metrics
    print("\nAlignment Metrics Comparison:")
    print("\nWell-Aligned Pairs:")
    aligned_metrics = compute_alignment_metrics(aligned_emb1, aligned_emb2)
    for key, value in aligned_metrics.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value:.4f}")
    
    print("\nMisaligned Pairs:")
    misaligned_metrics = compute_alignment_metrics(misaligned_emb1, misaligned_emb2)
    for key, value in misaligned_metrics.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value:.4f}")
    
    # Analyze alignment distribution
    print("\nAlignment Distribution Analysis:")
    aligned_sims = F.cosine_similarity(aligned_emb1, aligned_emb2, dim=-1)
    misaligned_sims = F.cosine_similarity(misaligned_emb1, misaligned_emb2, dim=-1)
    
    print(f"  Aligned - Mean: {aligned_sims.mean():.4f}, Std: {aligned_sims.std():.4f}")
    print(f"  Misaligned - Mean: {misaligned_sims.mean():.4f}, Std: {misaligned_sims.std():.4f}")
    
    # Separability analysis
    threshold = 0.5
    aligned_correct = (aligned_sims > threshold).float().mean()
    misaligned_correct = (misaligned_sims <= threshold).float().mean()
    
    print(f"\nSeparability at threshold {threshold}:")
    print(f"  Aligned pairs correctly identified: {aligned_correct.item():.2%}")
    print(f"  Misaligned pairs correctly identified: {misaligned_correct.item():.2%}\n")
