# 3032. Data Quality Versioning Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Version and track data quality metrics over time
Use Case: Quality monitoring, regression detection, and improvement tracking
"""

class DataQualityVersioning:
    """
    Tracks data quality metrics across versions.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, quality_dir: str = "./data_quality"):
        self.quality_dir = Path(quality_dir)
        self.quality_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```python
        self.quality_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.quality_reports = {}
    
    def compute_quality_metrics(self,
                               data: torch.Tensor,
                               data_id: str,
                               version: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Compute comprehensive quality metrics for data
        
        Args:
            data: Data tensor to analyze
            data_id: Data identifier
            version: Version identifier
        
        Returns:
            Quality metrics dictionary
        """
        metrics = {
            "data_id": data_id,
            "version": version,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "completeness": {},
            "validity": {},
            "consistency": {},
            "accuracy": {}
        }
        
        # Completeness metrics
        total_elements = data.numel()
        nan_count = torch.isnan(data.float()).sum().item()
        inf_count = torch.isinf(data.float()).sum().item()
        
        metrics["completeness"] = {
            "total_elements": total_elements,
            "missing_count": nan_count,
            "infinite_count": inf_count,
            "completeness_rate": 1.0 - (nan_count / total_elements) if total_elements > 0 else 0.0
        }
        
        # Validity metrics
        valid_data = data[~torch.isnan(data.float()) & ~torch.isinf(data.float())]
        
        if valid_data.numel() > 0:
            metrics["validity"] = {
                "min": valid_data.min().item(),
                "max": valid_data.max().item(),
                "mean": valid_data.float().mean().item(),
                "std": valid_data.float().std().item(),
                "median": valid_data.float().median().item()
            }
        
        # Consistency metrics (distribution properties)
        if valid_data.numel() > 1:
            # Compute quartiles
            quartiles = torch.quantile(valid_data.float(), torch.tensor([0.25, 0.5, 0.75]))
            iqr = quartiles[2] - quartiles[0]
            
            # Detect outliers using IQR method
            lower_bound = quartiles[0] - 1.5 * iqr
            upper_bound = quartiles[2] + 1.5 * iqr
            outliers = ((valid_data < lower_bound) | (valid_data > upper_bound)).sum().item()
            
            metrics["consistency"] = {
                "q1": quartiles[0].item(),
                "q2": quartiles[1].item(),
                "q3": quartiles[2].item(),
                "iqr": iqr.item(),
                "outlier_count": outliers,
                "outlier_rate": outliers / valid_data.numel()
            }
        
        # Overall quality score (0-1)
        quality_score = (
            metrics["completeness"]["completeness_rate"] * 0.4 +
            (1.0 - metrics["consistency"].get("outlier_rate", 0.0)) * 0.3 +
            0.3  # Base score for validity
        )
        
        metrics["overall_quality_score"] = quality_score
        
        # Store report
        report_id = f"{data_id}_v{version}"
        self.quality_reports[report_id] = metrics
        
        # Save to disk
        report_path = self.quality_dir / f"{report_id}_quality.json"
        with open(report_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Computed quality metrics for {report_id} (score: {quality_score:.3f})")
        return metrics
    
    def compare_quality(self,
                       version1: str,
                       version2: str,
                       data_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Compare quality metrics between two versions
        
        Args:
            version1: First version
            version2: Second version
            data_id: Data identifier
        
        Returns:
            Comparison report
        """
        report_id1 = f"{data_id}_v{version1}"
        report_id2 = f"{data_id}_v{version2}"
        
        if report_id1 not in self.quality_reports or report_id2 not in self.quality_reports:
            raise ValueError("One or both quality reports not found")
        
        metrics1 = self.quality_reports[report_id1]
        metrics2 = self.quality_reports[report_id2]
        
        comparison = {
            "version1": version1,
            "version2": version2,
            "quality_score_diff": metrics2["overall_quality_score"] - metrics1["overall_quality_score"],
            "completeness_diff": (
                metrics2["completeness"]["completeness_rate"] - 
                metrics1["completeness"]["completeness_rate"]
            ),
            "outlier_rate_diff": (
                metrics2["consistency"].get("outlier_rate", 0) - 
                metrics1["consistency"].get("outlier_rate", 0)
            ),
            "improved": metrics2["overall_quality_score"] > metrics1["overall_quality_score"]
        }
        
        return comparison
    
    def get_quality_trend(self, data_id: str) -> List[Dict]:
        """Get quality trend across all versions"""
        trend = []
        
        for report_id, metrics in self.quality_reports.items():
            if metrics["data_id"] == data_id:
                trend.append({
                    "version": metrics["version"],
                    "timestamp": metrics["timestamp"],
                    "quality_score": metrics["overall_quality_score"],
                    "completeness_rate": metrics["completeness"]["completeness_rate"]
                })
        
        return sorted(trend, key=lambda x: x["timestamp"])


# ============================================================================
# 3033. Experiment Tracking Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Track ML experiments with parameters, metrics, and artifacts
Use Case: Reproducibility, comparison, and experiment management
"""

class ExperimentTracker:
    """
    Comprehensive experiment tracking system for ML workflows.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, experiment_dir: str = "./experiments"):
        self.experiment_dir = Path(experiment_dir)
        self.experiment_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.experiments = {}
        self.active_experiment = None
    
    def start_experiment(self,
                        experiment_name: str,
                        description: str = "",
                        tags: List[str] = None) -> str:
        """
        Start a new experiment
        
        Args:
            experiment_name: Name of the experiment
            description: Experiment description
            tags: Tags for categorization
        
        Returns:
            Experiment ID
        """
        experiment_id = f"{experiment_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
        experiment_path = self.experiment_dir / experiment_id
        experiment_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        experiment_record = {
            "experiment_id": experiment_id,
            "experiment_name": experiment_name,
            "description": description,
            "tags": tags or [],
            "start_time": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "end_time": None,
            "status": "running",
            "parameters": {},
            "metrics": {},
            "artifacts": [],
            "logs": []
        }
        
        self.experiments[experiment_id] = experiment_record
        self.active_experiment = experiment_id
        
        print(f"✓ Started experiment '{experiment_id}'")
        return experiment_id
    
    def log_parameters(self, parameters: Dict[str, Any], experiment_id: str = None):
        """
        Log experiment parameters
        
        Args:
            parameters: Dictionary of parameters
            experiment_id: Optional experiment ID (uses active if not provided)
        """
        exp_id = experiment_id or self.active_experiment
        if exp_id is None:
            raise ValueError("No active experiment")
        
        self.experiments[exp_id]["parameters"].update(parameters)
        self._save_experiment(exp_id)
        
        print(f"✓ Logged {len(parameters)} parameters")
    
    def log_metrics(self,
                   metrics: Dict[str, float],
                   step: int = None,
                   experiment_id: str = None):
        """
        Log experiment metrics
        
        Args:
            metrics: Dictionary of metrics
            step: Optional step/epoch number
            experiment_id: Optional experiment ID
        """
        exp_id = experiment_id or self.active_experiment
        if exp_id is None:
            raise ValueError("No active experiment")
        
        timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        for metric_name, value in metrics.items():
            if metric_name not in self.experiments[exp_id]["metrics"]:
                self.experiments[exp_id]["metrics"][metric_name] = []
            
            self.experiments[exp_id]["metrics"][metric_name].append({
                "value": value,
                "step": step,
                "timestamp": timestamp
            })
        
        self._save_experiment(exp_id)
    
    def log_artifact(self,
                    artifact_name: str,
                    artifact_data: Any,
                    artifact_type: str = "tensor",
                    experiment_id: str = None):
        """
        Log an experiment artifact
        
        Args:
            artifact_name: Name of the artifact
            artifact_data: Artifact data (tensor, model, etc.)
            artifact_type: Type of artifact
            experiment_id: Optional experiment ID
        """
        exp_id = experiment_id or self.active_experiment
        if exp_id is None:
            raise ValueError("No active experiment")
        
        # Save artifact
        artifact_dir = self.experiment_dir / exp_id / "artifacts"
        artifact_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        artifact_path = artifact_dir / f"{artifact_name}.pt"
        
        if artifact_type == "tensor":
            torch.save(artifact_data, artifact_path)
        elif artifact_type == "model":
            torch.save(artifact_data.state_dict(), artifact_path)
        else:
            with open(artifact_path, 'wb') as f:
                pickle.dump(artifact_data, f)
        
        # Record artifact metadata
        artifact_record = {
            "name": artifact_name,
            "type": artifact_type,
            "path": str(artifact_path),
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.experiments[exp_id]["artifacts"].append(artifact_record)
        self._save_experiment(exp_id)
        
        print(f"✓ Logged artifact '{artifact_name}'")
    
    def log_message(self, message: str, level: str = "INFO", experiment_id: str = None):
        """
        Log a message
        
        Args:
            message: Log message
            level: Log level (INFO, WARNING, ERROR)
            experiment_id: Optional experiment ID
        """
        exp_id = experiment_id or self.active_experiment
        if exp_id is None:
            raise ValueError("No active experiment")
        
        log_entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "level": level,
            "message": message
        }
        
        self.experiments[exp_id]["logs"].append(log_entry)
        self._save_experiment(exp_id)
    
    def end_experiment(self, experiment_id: str = None, status: str = "completed"):
        """
        End an experiment
        
        Args:
            experiment_id: Optional experiment ID
            status: Final status (completed, failed, stopped)
        """
        exp_id = experiment_id or self.active_experiment
        if exp_id is None:
            raise ValueError("No active experiment")
        
        self.experiments[exp_id]["end_time"] = datetime.now().isoformat()
        self.experiments[exp_id]["status"] = status
        self._save_experiment(exp_id)
        
        if exp_id == self.active_experiment:
            self.active_experiment = None
        
        print(f"✓ Ended experiment '{exp_id}' with status '{status}'")
    
    def _save_experiment(self, experiment_id: str):
        """Save experiment record to disk"""
        exp_path = self.experiment_dir / experiment_id / "experiment.json"
        with open(exp_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.experiments[experiment_id], f, indent=2)
    
    def compare_experiments(self, experiment_ids: List[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Compare multiple experiments
        
        Args:
            experiment_ids: List of experiment IDs to compare
        
        Returns:
            Comparison report
        """
        comparison = {
            "experiments": [],
            "parameter_diff": {},
            "metric_comparison": {}
        }
        
        for exp_id in experiment_ids:
            if exp_id not in self.experiments:
                continue
            
            exp = self.experiments[exp_id]
            comparison["experiments"].append({
                "experiment_id": exp_id,
                "name": exp["experiment_name"],
                "status": exp["status"],
                "parameters": exp["parameters"]
            })
            
            # Collect final metrics
            for metric_name, values in exp["metrics"].items():
                if metric_name not in comparison["metric_comparison"]:
                    comparison["metric_comparison"][metric_name] = {}
                
                if values:
                    comparison["metric_comparison"][metric_name][exp_id] = values[-1]["value"]
        
        return comparison
    
    def get_best_experiment(self, metric_name: str, mode: str = "max") -> Dict:
        """
        Find best experiment based on a metric
        
        Args:
            metric_name: Metric to optimize
            mode: 'max' or 'min'
        
        Returns:
            Best experiment record
        """
        best_exp = None
        best_value = float('-inf') if mode == "max" else float('inf')
        
        for exp_id, exp in self.experiments.items():
            if metric_name in exp["metrics"] and exp["metrics"][metric_name]:
                final_value = exp["metrics"][metric_name][-1]["value"]
                
                if mode == "max" and final_value > best_value:
                    best_value = final_value
                    best_exp = exp
                elif mode == "min" and final_value < best_value:
                    best_value = final_value
                    best_exp = exp
        
        return best_exp


# ============================================================================
# 3034. Model Lineage Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Track model training lineage including data, code, and parameters
Use Case: Model reproducibility, debugging, and governance
"""

class ModelLineageTracker:
    """
    Tracks complete lineage of model training including all dependencies.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, lineage_dir: str = "./model_lineage"):
        self.lineage_dir = Path(lineage_dir)
        self.lineage_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.model_records = {}
    
    def register_model(self,
                      model_id: str,
                      model: torch.nn.Module,
                      training_data_id: str,
                      hyperparameters: Dict,
                      training_code_hash: str = "",
                      parent_model_id: Optional[str] = None,
                      metadata: Dict = None) -> str
```python
                      metadata: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        Register a trained model with complete lineage
        
        Args:
            model_id: Unique model identifier
            model: PyTorch model
            training_data_id: ID of training data
            hyperparameters: Training hyperparameters
            training_code_hash: Hash of training code
            parent_model_id: ID of parent model (for fine-tuning, etc.)
            metadata: Additional metadata
        
        Returns:
            Model ID
        """
        model_path = self.lineage_dir / model_id
        model_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        # Save model
        model_file = model_path / "model.pt"
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), model_file)
        
        # Compute model hash
        model_hash = hashlib.sha256(
            str(model.state_dict()).encode()
        ).hexdigest()
        
        # Create lineage record
        lineage_record = {
            "model_id": model_id,
            "model_hash": model_hash,
            "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "architecture": {
                "type": type(model).__name__,
                "num_parameters": sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()),
                "trainable_parameters": sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
            },
            "training": {
                "data_id": training_data_id,
                "hyperparameters": hyperparameters,
                "code_hash": training_code_hash
            },
            "lineage": {
                "parent_model_id": parent_model_id,
                "training_type": "fine-tuned" if parent_model_id else "from-scratch"
            },
            "metadata": metadata or {},
            "dependencies": []
        }
        
        self.model_records[model_id] = lineage_record
        
        # Save lineage record
        lineage_file = model_path / "lineage.json"
        with open(lineage_file, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(lineage_record, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Registered model '{model_id}' with hash {model_hash[:8]}...")
        return model_id
    
    def add_dependency(self,
                      model_id: str,
                      dependency_type: str,
                      dependency_id: str,
                      dependency_version: str = ""):
        """
        Add a dependency to model lineage
        
        Args:
            model_id: Model identifier
            dependency_type: Type of dependency (data, library, model, etc.)
            dependency_id: Dependency identifier
            dependency_version: Version of dependency
        """
        if model_id not in self.model_records:
            raise ValueError(f"Model '{model_id}' not found")
        
        dependency = {
            "type": dependency_type,
            "id": dependency_id,
            "version": dependency_version,
            "added_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.model_records[model_id]["dependencies"].append(dependency)
        
        # Update saved record
        model_path = self.lineage_dir / model_id
        lineage_file = model_path / "lineage.json"
        with open(lineage_file, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.model_records[model_id], f, indent=2)
    
    def get_model_lineage(self, model_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Get complete lineage for a model"""
        if model_id not in self.model_records:
            raise ValueError(f"Model '{model_id}' not found")
        
        return self.model_records[model_id]
    
    def trace_ancestry(self, model_id: str) -> List[str]:
        """
        Trace model ancestry back to original model
        
        Args:
            model_id: Model identifier
        
        Returns:
            List of model IDs from current to root
        """
        ancestry = [model_id]
        current_id = model_id
        
        while current_id in self.model_records:
            parent_id = self.model_records[current_id]["lineage"].get("parent_model_id")
            if parent_id is None:
                break
            ancestry.append(parent_id)
            current_id = parent_id
        
        return ancestry
    
    def compare_models(self, model_id1: str, model_id2: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Compare two models
        
        Args:
            model_id1: First model ID
            model_id2: Second model ID
        
        Returns:
            Comparison report
        """
        if model_id1 not in self.model_records or model_id2 not in self.model_records:
            raise ValueError("One or both models not found")
        
        record1 = self.model_records[model_id1]
        record2 = self.model_records[model_id2]
        
        comparison = {
            "model1": model_id1,
            "model2": model_id2,
            "same_architecture": record1["architecture"]["type"] == record2["architecture"]["type"],
            "parameter_diff": (
                record2["architecture"]["num_parameters"] - 
                record1["architecture"]["num_parameters"]
            ),
            "same_training_data": (
                record1["training"]["data_id"] == record2["training"]["data_id"]
            ),
            "hyperparameter_diff": self._diff_dicts(
                record1["training"]["hyperparameters"],
                record2["training"]["hyperparameters"]
            ),
            "share_common_ancestor": bool(
                set(self.trace_ancestry(model_id1)) & set(self.trace_ancestry(model_id2))
            )
        }
        
        return comparison
    
    def _diff_dicts(self, dict1: Dict, dict2: Dict) -> Dict:
        """Find differences between two dictionaries"""
        diff = {
            "added": {},
            "removed": {},
            "changed": {}
        }
        
        all_keys = set(dict1.keys()) | set(dict2.keys())
        
        for key in all_keys:
            if key not in dict1:
                diff["added"][key] = dict2[key]
            elif key not in dict2:
                diff["removed"][key] = dict1[key]
            elif dict1[key] != dict2[key]:
                diff["changed"][key] = {
                    "old": dict1[key],
                    "new": dict2[key]
                }
        
        return diff


# ============================================================================
# 3035. Artifact Tracking Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Track all artifacts produced during ML workflow
Use Case: Organization, versioning, and retrieval of ML artifacts
"""

class ArtifactTracker:
    """
    Centralized tracking system for ML artifacts.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, artifact_dir: str = "./artifacts"):
        self.artifact_dir = Path(artifact_dir)
        self.artifact_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.artifacts = {}
        self.artifact_counter = 0
    
    def register_artifact(self,
                         artifact_name: str,
                         artifact_type: str,
                         artifact_data: Any,
                         producer: str = "",
                         tags: List[str] = None,
                         metadata: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        Register a new artifact
        
        Args:
            artifact_name: Name of the artifact
            artifact_type: Type (model, dataset, plot, metric, etc.)
            artifact_data: The actual artifact
            producer: Who/what produced this artifact
            tags: Tags for categorization
            metadata: Additional metadata
        
        Returns:
            Artifact ID
        """
        self.artifact_counter += 1
        artifact_id = f"artifact_{self.artifact_counter}_{artifact_name}"
        
        artifact_path = self.artifact_dir / artifact_id
        artifact_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        # Save artifact based on type
        if artifact_type == "model":
            save_path = artifact_path / "artifact.pt"
            torch.save(artifact_data.state_dict(), save_path)
        elif artifact_type == "tensor":
            save_path = artifact_path / "artifact.pt"
            torch.save(artifact_data, save_path)
        elif artifact_type == "plot":
            save_path = artifact_path / "artifact.png"
            artifact_data.savefig(save_path)
        else:
            save_path = artifact_path / "artifact.pkl"
            with open(save_path, 'wb') as f:
                pickle.dump(artifact_data, f)
        
        # Create artifact record
        artifact_record = {
            "artifact_id": artifact_id,
            "artifact_name": artifact_name,
            "artifact_type": artifact_type,
            "producer": producer,
            "tags": tags or [],
            "metadata": metadata or {},
            "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "path": str(save_path),
            "size_bytes": save_path.stat().st_size if save_path.exists() else 0
        }
        
        self.artifacts[artifact_id] = artifact_record
        
        # Save artifact metadata
        metadata_path = artifact_path / "metadata.json"
        with open(metadata_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(artifact_record, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Registered artifact '{artifact_id}'")
        return artifact_id
    
    def get_artifact(self, artifact_id: str) -> Any:
        """
        Retrieve an artifact
        
        Args:
            artifact_id: Artifact identifier
        
        Returns:
            Artifact data
        """
        if artifact_id not in self.artifacts:
            raise ValueError(f"Artifact '{artifact_id}' not found")
        
        record = self.artifacts[artifact_id]
        artifact_path = Path(record["path"])
        
        # Load based on type
        if record["artifact_type"] in ["model", "tensor"]:
            return torch.load(artifact_path)
        else:
            with open(artifact_path, 'rb') as f:
                return pickle.load(f)
    
    def search_artifacts(self,
                        artifact_type: str = None,
                        tags: List[str] = None,
                        producer: str = None) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Search artifacts by criteria
        
        Args:
            artifact_type: Filter by type
            tags: Filter by tags
            producer: Filter by producer
        
        Returns:
            List of matching artifact records
        """
        results = []
        
        for artifact_id, record in self.artifacts.items():
            match = True
            
            if artifact_type and record["artifact_type"] != artifact_type:
                match = False
            
            if tags and not any(tag in record["tags"] for tag in tags):
                match = False
            
            if producer and record["producer"] != producer:
                match = False
            
            if match:
                results.append(record)
        
        return results
    
    def link_artifacts(self,
                      source_artifact_id: str,
                      target_artifact_id: str,
                      relationship: str):
        """
        Create a relationship between artifacts
        
        Args:
            source_artifact_id: Source artifact ID
            target_artifact_id: Target artifact ID
            relationship: Type of relationship (e.g., 'derived_from', 'uses', 'produces')
        """
        if source_artifact_id not in self.artifacts or target_artifact_id not in self.artifacts:
            raise ValueError("One or both artifacts not found")
        
        if "relationships" not in self.artifacts[source_artifact_id]:
            self.artifacts[source_artifact_id]["relationships"] = []
        
        relationship_record = {
            "target": target_artifact_id,
            "type": relationship,
            "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.artifacts[source_artifact_id]["relationships"].append(relationship_record)
        
        # Update metadata file
        artifact_path = self.artifact_dir / source_artifact_id
        metadata_path = artifact_path / "metadata.json"
        with open(metadata_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(self.artifacts[source_artifact_id], f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Linked {source_artifact_id} -> {target_artifact_id} ({relationship})")
    
    def get_artifact_graph(self, artifact_id: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Get relationship graph for an artifact
        
        Args:
            artifact_id: Artifact identifier
        
        Returns:
            Graph structure
        """
        if artifact_id not in self.artifacts:
            raise ValueError(f"Artifact '{artifact_id}' not found")
        
        graph = {
            "root": artifact_id,
            "relationships": self.artifacts[artifact_id].get("relationships", [])
        }
        
        return graph

"""
Pattern: Ensure complete reproducibility of ML experiments
Use Case: Scientific rigor, debugging, and result verification
"""

class ReproducibilityManager:
    """
    Manages all aspects of experiment reproducibility.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, repro_dir: str = "./reproducibility"):
        self.repro_dir = Path(repro_dir)
        self.repro_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.snapshots = {}
    
    def create_reproducibility_snapshot(self,
                                       snapshot_name: str,
                                       model: torch.nn.Module,
                                       optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,

                                       environment: Dict) -> str:

            model: PyTorch model
            optimizer: Optimizer
            random_state: Random number generator states
            data_version: Version of data used
            code_hash: Hash of training code
            environment: Environment information
        
        Returns:
            Snapshot ID
        """
        snapshot_id = f"{snapshot_name}_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}"
        snapshot_path = self.repro_dir / snapshot_id
        snapshot_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        # Save model
        torch.save(model.state_dict(), snapshot_path / "model.pt")
        
        # Save optimizer
        torch.save(optimizer.state_dict(), snapshot_path / "optimizer.pt")
        
        # Save random states
        torch.save(random_state, snapshot_path / "random_state.pt")
        
        # Create snapshot record
        snapshot_record = {
            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
            "snapshot_name": snapshot_name,
            "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "model_architecture": str(model),
            "optimizer_type": type(optimizer).__name__,
            "data_version": data_version,
            "code_hash": code_hash,
            "environment": environment,
            "pytorch_version": torch.__version__,
            "random_state_keys": list(random_state.keys())
        }
        
        self.snapshots[snapshot_id] = snapshot_record
        
        # Save snapshot metadata
        with open(snapshot_path /
```python
        with open(snapshot_path / "snapshot.json", 'w') as f:
            json.dump(snapshot_record, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Created reproducibility snapshot '{snapshot_id}'")
        return snapshot_id
    
    def restore_snapshot(self,
                        snapshot_id: str,
                        model: torch.nn.Module,
                        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer) -> Dict:
        """
        Restore from a reproducibility snapshot
        
        Args:
            snapshot_id: Snapshot identifier
            model: Model to restore state into
            optimizer: Optimizer to restore state into
        
        Returns:
            Random state dictionary
        """
        snapshot_path = self.repro_dir / snapshot_id
        
        if not snapshot_path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f"Snapshot '{snapshot_id}' not found")
        
        # Restore model
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(snapshot_path / "model.pt"))
        
        # Restore optimizer
        optimizer.load_state_dict(torch.load(snapshot_path / "optimizer.pt"))
        
        # Load random state
        random_state = torch.load(snapshot_path / "random_state.pt")
        
        print(f"✓ Restored snapshot '{snapshot_id}'")
        return random_state
    
    def verify_reproducibility(self,
                              snapshot_id: str,
                              current_environment: Dict) -> Dict:
        """
        Verify if current environment matches snapshot
        
        Args:
            snapshot_id: Snapshot to verify against
            current_environment: Current environment info
        
        Returns:
            Verification report
        """
        if snapshot_id not in self.snapshots:
            raise ValueError(f"Snapshot '{snapshot_id}' not found")
        
        snapshot = self.snapshots[snapshot_id]
        
        verification = {
            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id,
            "verified_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "matches": {},
            "differences": {},
            "reproducible": True
        }
        
        # Check PyTorch version
        if snapshot["pytorch_version"] != torch.__version__:
            verification["differences"]["pytorch_version"] = {
                "snapshot": snapshot["pytorch_version"],
                "current": torch.__version__
            }
            verification["reproducible"] = False
        
        # Check environment variables
        snapshot_env = snapshot["environment"]
        for key in snapshot_env:
            if key in current_environment:
                if snapshot_env[key] != current_environment[key]:
                    verification["differences"][key] = {
                        "snapshot": snapshot_env[key],
                        "current": current_environment[key]
                    }
                    verification["reproducible"] = False
                else:
                    verification["matches"][key] = snapshot_env[key]
            else:
                verification["differences"][key] = {
                    "snapshot": snapshot_env[key],
                    "current": None
                }
                verification["reproducible"] = False
        
        return verification
    
    def export_reproduction_script(self,
                                   snapshot_id: str,
                                   output_path: str):
        """
        Export a script to reproduce the experiment
        
        Args:
            snapshot_id: Snapshot identifier
            output_path: Path to save script
        """
        if snapshot_id not in self.snapshots:
            raise ValueError(f"Snapshot '{snapshot_id}' not found")
        
        snapshot = self.snapshots[snapshot_id]
        
        script_lines = [
            "#!/usr/bin/env python3",
            "# Auto-generated reproduction script",
            f"# Snapshot: {snapshot_id}",
            f"# Created: {snapshot['created_at']}",
            "",
            "import torch",
            "import random",
            "import numpy as np",
            "",
            "# Set random seeds for reproducibility",
            "def set_seed(seed=42):",
            "    torch.manual_seed(seed)",
            "    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)",
            "    np.random.seed(seed)",
            "    random.seed(seed)",
            "    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True",
            "    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False",
            "",
            "# Environment requirements:",
            f"# PyTorch version: {snapshot['pytorch_version']}",
        ]
        
        for key, value in snapshot["environment"].items():
            script_lines.append(f"# {key}: {value}")
        
        script_lines.extend([
            "",
            "# Initialize random state",
            "set_seed(42)",
            "",
            f"# Load snapshot from: {self.repro_dir / snapshot_id}",
            "# Follow the original training procedure with the same:",
            f"# - Data version: {snapshot['data_version']}",
            f"# - Code hash: {snapshot['code_hash']}",
            f"# - Optimizer: {snapshot['optimizer_type']}",
        ])
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write("\n".join(script_lines))
        
        print(f"✓ Exported reproduction script to {output_path}")


# ============================================================================
# 3037. Deterministic Training Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Ensure deterministic training for reproducibility
Use Case: Debugging, testing, and reproducible research
"""

class DeterministicTraining:
    """
    Utilities for ensuring deterministic training in PyTorch.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, seed: int = 42):
        self.seed = seed
        self.original_settings = {}
    
    def enable_deterministic_mode(self):
        """
        Enable deterministic mode for PyTorch
        """
        # Store original settings
        self.original_settings = {
            "cudnn_deterministic": torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic,
            "cudnn_benchmark": torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark
        }
        
        # Set deterministic flags
        torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
        torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
        
        # Set environment variables for deterministic algorithms
        import os
        os.environ['CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG'] = ':4096:8'
        
        # Enable PyTorch deterministic algorithms (if available)
        try:
            torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
        except AttributeError:
            # Older PyTorch versions
            pass
        
        print("✓ Enabled deterministic mode")
    
    def disable_deterministic_mode(self):
        """
        Restore original settings
        """
        if self.original_settings:
            torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = self.original_settings["cudnn_deterministic"]
            torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = self.original_settings["cudnn_benchmark"]
        
        try:
            torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(False)
        except AttributeError:
            pass
        
        print("✓ Disabled deterministic mode")
    
    def set_global_seed(self, seed: Optional[int] = None):
        """
        Set seed for all random number generators
        
        Args:
            seed: Random seed (uses instance seed if not provided)
        """
        seed = seed or self.seed
        
        # PyTorch
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
        
        # Python
        import random
        random.seed(seed)
        
        # NumPy
        try:
            import numpy as np
            np.random.seed(seed)
        except ImportError:
            pass
        
        print(f"✓ Set global seed to {seed}")
    
    def get_random_state(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Capture current random state
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary of random states
        """
        import random
        
        state = {
            "torch_cpu": torch.get_rng_state(),
            "python": random.getstate(),
        }
        
        # CUDA states
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            state["torch_cuda"] = torch.cuda.get_rng_state_all()
        
        # NumPy state
        try:
            import numpy as np
            state["numpy"] = np.random.get_state()
        except ImportError:
            pass
        
        return state
    
    def set_random_state(self, state: Dict):
        """
        Restore random state
        
        Args:
            state: Dictionary of random states
        """
        import random
        
        # PyTorch CPU
        if "torch_cpu" in state:
            torch.set_rng_state(state["torch_cpu"])
        
        # PyTorch CUDA
        if "torch_cuda" in state and torch.cuda.is_available():
            torch.cuda.set_rng_state_all(state["torch_cuda"])
        
        # Python
        if "python" in state:
            random.setstate(state["python"])
        
        # NumPy
        if "numpy" in state:
            try:
                import numpy as np
                np.random.set_state(state["numpy"])
            except ImportError:
                pass
        
        print("✓ Restored random state")
    
    def create_deterministic_dataloader(self,
                                       dataset: torch.utils.data.Dataset,
                                       batch_size: int,
                                       **kwargs) -> torch.utils.data.DataLoader:
        """
        Create a deterministic DataLoader
        
        Args:
            dataset: PyTorch dataset
            batch_size: Batch size
            **kwargs: Additional DataLoader arguments
        
        Returns:
            Deterministic DataLoader
        """
        # Set worker init function for deterministic workers
        def worker_init_fn(worker_id):
            worker_seed = self.seed + worker_id
            import random
            random.seed(worker_seed)
            try:
                import numpy as np
                np.random.seed(worker_seed)
            except ImportError:
                pass
        
        # Create DataLoader with deterministic settings
        dataloader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
            dataset,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            worker_init_fn=worker_init_fn,
            generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(self.seed),
            **kwargs
        )
        
        return dataloader


# ============================================================================
# 3038. Seed Management Pattern
# ============================================================================
"""
Pattern: Manage random seeds across experiments
Use Case: Reproducibility with multiple runs and cross-validation
"""

class SeedManager:
    """
    Manages random seeds for experiments with multiple runs.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_seed: int = 42):
        self.base_seed = base_seed
        self.seed_registry = {}
        self.current_seeds = {}
    
    def register_component(self, component_name: str, seed_offset: int = 0):
        """
        Register a component with a specific seed offset
        
        Args:
            component_name: Name of the component
            seed_offset: Offset from base seed
        """
        seed = self.base_seed + seed_offset
        self.seed_registry[component_name] = seed
        
        print(f"✓ Registered component '{component_name}' with seed {seed}")
    
    def get_seed(self, component_name: str, run_id: int = 0) -> int:
        """
        Get seed for a component and run
        
        Args:
            component_name: Name of the component
            run_id: Run identifier
        
        Returns:
            Seed value
        """
        if component_name not in self.seed_registry:
            raise ValueError(f"Component '{component_name}' not registered")
        
        base_seed = self.seed_registry[component_name]
        seed = base_seed + (run_id * 10000)  # Large offset between runs
        
        return seed
    
    def create_seed_schedule(self,
                            num_runs: int,
                            components: List[str]) -> Dict[int, Dict[str, int]]:
        """
        Create a seed schedule for multiple runs
        
        Args:
            num_runs: Number of runs
            components: List of component names
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping run_id to component seeds
        """
        schedule = {}
        
        for run_id in range(num_runs):
            schedule[run_id] = {}
            for component in components:
                schedule[run_id][component] = self.get_seed(component, run_id)
        
        return schedule
    
    def save_seed_schedule(self, schedule: Dict, filepath: str):
        """Save seed schedule to file"""
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(schedule, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Saved seed schedule to {filepath}")
    
    def load_seed_schedule(self, filepath: str) -> Dict:
        """Load seed schedule from file"""
        with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
            schedule = json.load(f)
        
        # Convert string keys back to integers
        schedule = {int(k): v for k, v in schedule.items()}
        
        print(f"✓ Loaded seed schedule from {filepath}")
        return schedule
    
    def apply_seeds(self, component_seeds: Dict[str, int]):
        """
        Apply seeds to all components
        
        Args:
            component_seeds: Dictionary mapping component names to seeds
        """
        import random
        
        for component, seed in component_seeds.items():
            torch.manual_seed(seed)
            random.seed(seed)
            try:

            self.current_seeds[component] = seed
        
        print(f"✓ Applied seeds for {len(component_seeds)} components")

    def capture_environment(self, env_name: str) -> str:
        """

        Args:
            env_name: Name for this environment
        
        Returns:
            Environment ID
        """

        # Capture environment details
        env_info = {

            "env_name": env_name,

                "implementation": platform.python_implementation(),
                "compiler": platform.python_compiler()
            },

            },
            "pytorch": {
                "version": torch.__version__,
                "cuda_available": torch.cuda.is_available(),
                "cuda_version": torch.version.cuda if torch.cuda.is_available() else None,

            },
            "packages": self._get_installed_packages()
```python
            "packages": self._get_installed_packages()
        }
        
        # Add CUDA device information if available
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            env_info["cuda_devices"] = []
            for i in range(torch.cuda.device_count()):
                env_info["cuda_devices"].append({
                    "id": i,
                    "name": torch.cuda.get_device_name(i),
                    "capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(i),
                    "total_memory": torch.cuda.get_device_properties(i).total_memory
                })
        
        self.environments[env_id] = env_info
        
        # Save environment info
        env_path = self.env_dir / f"{env_id}.json"
        with open(env_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(env_info, f, indent=2)
        
        # Export requirements.txt
        self._export_requirements(env_id)
        
        print(f"✓ Captured environment '{env_id}'")
        return env_id
    
    def _get_installed_packages(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """Get installed Python packages"""
        try:
            import pkg_resources
            packages = {}
            for dist in pkg_resources.working_set:
                packages[dist.project_name] = dist.version
            return packages
        except ImportError:
            return {}
    
    def _export_requirements(self, env_id: str):
        """Export requirements.txt for environment"""
        if env_id not in self.environments:
            return
        
        env_info = self.environments[env_id]
        requirements_path = self.env_dir / f"{env_id}_requirements.txt"
        
        with open(requirements_path, 'w') as f:
            for package, version in sorted(env_info["packages"].items()):
                f.write(f"{package}=={version}\n")
        
        print(f"✓ Exported requirements to {requirements_path}")
    
    def compare_environments(self, env_id1: str, env_id2: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Compare two environments
        
        Args:
            env_id1: First environment ID
            env_id2: Second environment ID
        
        Returns:
            Comparison report
        """
        if env_id1 not in self.environments or env_id2 not in self.environments:
            raise ValueError("One or both environments not found")
        
        env1 = self.environments[env_id1]
        env2 = self.environments[env_id2]
        
        comparison = {
            "env1": env_id1,
            "env2": env_id2,
            "python_version_match": env1["python"]["version"] == env2["python"]["version"],
            "pytorch_version_match": env1["pytorch"]["version"] == env2["pytorch"]["version"],
            "system_match": env1["system"]["platform"] == env2["system"]["platform"],
            "package_differences": {}
        }
        
        # Compare packages
        packages1 = set(env1["packages"].keys())
        packages2 = set(env2["packages"].keys())
        
        comparison["package_differences"] = {
            "only_in_env1": list(packages1 - packages2),
            "only_in_env2": list(packages2 - packages1),
            "version_mismatch": []
        }
        
        # Check version mismatches
        for package in packages1 & packages2:
            if env1["packages"][package] != env2["packages"][package]:
                comparison["package_differences"]["version_mismatch"].append({
                    "package": package,
                    "env1_version": env1["packages"][package],
                    "env2_version": env2["packages"][package]
                })
        
        return comparison
    
    def validate_environment(self, env_id: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Validate current environment against a saved environment
        
        Args:
            env_id: Environment ID to validate against
        
        Returns:
            Validation report
        """
        if env_id not in self.environments:
            raise ValueError(f"Environment '{env_id}' not found")
        
        # Capture current environment
        current_env_id = self.capture_environment("current_validation")
        
        # Compare with target environment
        comparison = self.compare_environments(env_id, current_env_id)
        
        validation = {
            "target_env": env_id,
            "validated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "is_compatible": True,
            "issues": []
        }
        
        # Check critical mismatches
        if not comparison["python_version_match"]:
            validation["is_compatible"] = False
            validation["issues"].append("Python version mismatch")
        
        if not comparison["pytorch_version_match"]:
            validation["is_compatible"] = False
            validation["issues"].append("PyTorch version mismatch")
        
        if comparison["package_differences"]["version_mismatch"]:
            validation["issues"].append(
                f"{len(comparison['package_differences']['version_mismatch'])} package version mismatches"
            )
        
        return validation
    
    def export_dockerfile(self, env_id: str, output_path: str):
        """
        Export a Dockerfile to recreate the environment
        
        Args:
            env_id: Environment ID
            output_path: Path to save Dockerfile
        """
        if env_id not in self.environments:
            raise ValueError(f"Environment '{env_id}' not found")
        
        env_info = self.environments[env_id]
        
        dockerfile_lines = [
            "# Auto-generated Dockerfile",
            f"# Environment: {env_id}",
            f"# Generated: {datetime.now().isoformat()}",
            "",
            f"FROM python:{env_info['python']['version'].split()[0]}-slim",
            "",
            "WORKDIR /app",
            "",
            "# Install system dependencies",
            "RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \\",
            "    build-essential \\",
            "    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*",
            "",
            "# Copy requirements",
            f"COPY {env_id}_requirements.txt requirements.txt",
            "",
            "# Install Python packages",
            "RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt",
            "",
            "# Copy application code",
            "COPY . .",
            "",
            "CMD [\"python\"]"
        ]
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write("\n".join(dockerfile_lines))
        
        print(f"✓ Exported Dockerfile to {output_path}")

"""
Pattern: Track all dependencies and their versions in ML workflows
Use Case: Reproducibility, security auditing, and dependency management
"""

class DependencyTracker:
    """
    Tracks all dependencies for ML projects including code, data, and models.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, dependency_dir: str = "./dependencies"):
        self.dependency_dir = Path(dependency_dir)
        self.dependency_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.dependency_graph = {}
        self.dependency_metadata = {}
    
    def register_dependency(self,
                          dependency_id: str,
                          dependency_type: str,
                          version: str,
                          source: str = "",
                          metadata: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        Register a dependency
        
        Args:
            dependency_id: Unique dependency identifier
            dependency_type: Type (package, model, data, code)
            version: Version identifier
            source: Source location or URL
            metadata: Additional metadata
        
        Returns:
            Dependency ID
        """
        dependency_record = {
            "dependency_id": dependency_id,
            "dependency_type": dependency_type,
            "version": version,
            "source": source,
            "registered_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "metadata": metadata or {},
            "dependents": [],
            "dependencies": []
        }
        
        self.dependency_metadata[dependency_id] = dependency_record
        
        if dependency_id not in self.dependency_graph:
            self.dependency_graph[dependency_id] = {
                "dependencies": [],
                "dependents": []
            }
        
        # Save dependency record
        dep_path = self.dependency_dir / f"{dependency_id}.json"
        with open(dep_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(dependency_record, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Registered dependency '{dependency_id}' v{version}")
        return dependency_id
    
    def add_dependency_relationship(self,
                                   dependent_id: str,
                                   dependency_id: str,
                                   relationship_type: str = "requires"):
        """
        Add a dependency relationship
        
        Args:
            dependent_id: ID of the dependent component
            dependency_id: ID of the dependency
            relationship_type: Type of relationship
        """
        if dependent_id not in self.dependency_graph:
            self.dependency_graph[dependent_id] = {
                "dependencies": [],
                "dependents": []
            }
        
        if dependency_id not in self.dependency_graph:
            self.dependency_graph[dependency_id] = {
                "dependencies": [],
                "dependents": []
            }
        
        # Add relationship
        relationship = {
            "id": dependency_id,
            "type": relationship_type,
            "added_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        if relationship not in self.dependency_graph[dependent_id]["dependencies"]:
            self.dependency_graph[dependent_id]["dependencies"].append(relationship)
        
        # Add reverse relationship
        reverse_relationship = {
            "id": dependent_id,
            "type": relationship_type,
            "added_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        if reverse_relationship not in self.dependency_graph[dependency_id]["dependents"]:
            self.dependency_graph[dependency_id]["dependents"].append(reverse_relationship)
        
        # Update metadata
        if dependent_id in self.dependency_metadata:
            if dependency_id not in self.dependency_metadata[dependent_id]["dependencies"]:
                self.dependency_metadata[dependent_id]["dependencies"].append(dependency_id)
        
        if dependency_id in self.dependency_metadata:
            if dependent_id not in self.dependency_metadata[dependency_id]["dependents"]:
                self.dependency_metadata[dependency_id]["dependents"].append(dependent_id)
        
        print(f"✓ Added dependency: {dependent_id} -> {dependency_id}")
    
    def get_dependencies(self, component_id: str, recursive: bool = False) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Get dependencies for a component
        
        Args:
            component_id: Component identifier
            recursive: Whether to get transitive dependencies
        
        Returns:
            List of dependencies
        """
        if component_id not in self.dependency_graph:
            return []
        
        dependencies = []
        visited = set()
        
        def collect_deps(comp_id):
            if comp_id in visited:
                return
            visited.add(comp_id)
            
            if comp_id in self.dependency_graph:
                for dep in self.dependency_graph[comp_id]["dependencies"]:
                    dep_id = dep["id"]
                    if dep_id in self.dependency_metadata:
                        dependencies.append(self.dependency_metadata[dep_id])
                    
                    if recursive:
                        collect_deps(dep_id)
        
        collect_deps(component_id)
        return dependencies
    
    def get_dependents(self, component_id: str) -> List[Dict]:
        """Get all components that depend on this component"""
        if component_id not in self.dependency_graph:
            return []
        
        dependents = []
        for dep in self.dependency_graph[component_id]["dependents"]:
            dep_id = dep["id"]
            if dep_id in self.dependency_metadata:
                dependents.append(self.dependency_metadata[dep_id])
        
        return dependents
    
    def check_circular_dependencies(self, component_id: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Check for circular dependencies
        
        Args:
            component_id: Component to check
        
        Returns:
            Report of circular dependencies
        """
        visited = set()
        path = []
        cycles = []
        
        def dfs(comp_id):
            if comp_id in path:
                # Found a cycle
                cycle_start = path.index(comp_id)
                cycles.append(path[cycle_start:] + [comp_id])
                return
            
            if comp_id in visited:
                return
            
            visited.add(comp_id)
            path.append(comp_id)
            
            if comp_id in self.dependency_graph:
                for dep in self.dependency_graph[comp_id]["dependencies"]:
                    dfs(dep["id"])
            
            path.pop()
        
        dfs(component_id)
        
        return {
            "component_id": component_id,
            "has_cycles": len(cycles) > 0,
            "cycles": cycles,
            "num_cycles": len(cycles)
        }
    
    def generate_dependency_tree(self, component_id: str, max_depth: int = 5) -> str:
        """
        Generate a text-based dependency tree
        
        Args:
            component_id: Root component
            max_depth: Maximum depth to traverse
        
        Returns:
            Tree string
        """
        lines = []
        visited = set()
        
        def build_tree(comp_id, depth=0, prefix=""):
            if depth > max_depth or comp_id in visited:
                return
            
            visited.add(comp_id)
            
            # Get component info
            comp_info = self.dependency_metadata.get(comp_id, {})
            version = comp_info.get("version", "unknown")
            dep_type = comp_info.get("dependency_type", "unknown")
            
            # Add line
            indent = "  " * depth
            lines.append(f"{indent}{prefix}{comp_id} (v{version}, {dep_type})")
            
            # Process dependencies
            if comp_id in self.dependency_graph:
                deps = self.dependency_graph[comp_id]["dependencies"]
                for i, dep in enumerate(deps):
                    is_last = i == len(deps) - 1
                    branch = "└─ " if is_last else "├─ "
                    build_tree(dep["id"], depth + 1, branch)
        
        build_tree(component_id)
        return "\n".join(lines)
    
    def export_dependency_graph(self, output_path: str, format: str = "json"):
        """
        Export dependency graph
        
        Args:
            output_path: Output file path
            format: Export format (json, dot)
        """
        if format == "json":
            export_data = {
                "metadata": self.dependency_metadata,
                "graph": self.dependency_graph,
                "exported_at": datetime.now().isoformat()
            }
            
            with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
                json.dump(export_data, f, indent=2)
        
        elif format == "dot":
            # GraphViz DOT format
            lines = ["digraph dependencies {"]
            lines.append("  rankdir=LR;")
            lines.append("  node [shape=box];")
